Review Title: Right side rewards, left side regrets.
Review Text: This sightseeing flight offered some beautiful views, but I found the experience heavily favored passengers on the right side of the aircraft. As a left-side passenger, my view was primarily of the shoreline, and I missed out on many of the central island's key attractions like the mountains, canyons, and waterfalls. To maximize your experience, I'd strongly recommend requesting a right-side seat. Additionally, strategically maneuvering the aircraft to provide brief, alternating views of key landmarks for both sides of the plane could help ensure a more equitable experience for all passengers.

Review Title: Great value, awesome pilot and wonderful views
Review Text:
I had been looking at this flight since we began planning our trip to Kauai, but was still on the fence . We did a helicopter tour of the Big Island 20 years ago and kept wondering if it was worth double the price to go on a helicopter here. On our first day we drove out to Waimea Canyon and there we made our choice. We saw the plane and a helicopter pass over us and decided the plane looked great.

We booked the flight online 10:30 am (later we heard a pilot share this was the best time but honestly I don't think you could go wrong either time. )

Got to the airport and checked in a little later our pilot Nick came by and welcomed us. Walked out to the plane did a little safety brief, low door watch your head and so on, then loaded the plane for the typical over the water flight, loved the bit of humor with the air sickness bag and taxid out to the runway.
Nick is a wonderful young pilot, those folks seem to be getting younger every year, or .aybe it's just me. Local guy, no doubt loves what he does and where he lives. Offered a great tour pointing out highlights and the coolest thing was making some left hand turns for those of us on the other side of the plane. Great pilot he banked us over so we could get some great pictures and did it so SMOOTHLY that we hardly noticed.
We took some incredible pictures and a few videos of the entire island. It was really cool having him point out places we had visited and see it from the air.
Wish there was a higher rating we could give. Highly recommend this trip 👌 best value and awesome views, what a combo!
Use my name when you get there they won't remember me just say little round guy big smile, grinned the rest of the day. Book it book it now
. Can't wait to come back and do it again.

Review Text:
My hour long tour was the "Big Kahuna Air Tour" and I was in the company of my wife.
The plane had room for 6 passengers in addition to the pilot, I was very eager to have this experience not only to see Kauai from above, but also to take photographs and video footage, which I am very passionate about.
Unfortunately, the pilot, without asking anything, placed both me and my wife in the second row, where on the side there is the bar that holds the wing of the plane.
I was on the left side, immediately behind the pilot.
During the flight, those on the right were greatly privileged. Traveling on the left you were always too close to the mountain without having an overall view, while on the right side you were always a little further away, allowing you to see much better.
I practically didn't see well the Napali Coast because we were very close to the mountain while when we went back, from the right side they could see well both the mountain and the sea below.
Not to mention the great annoyance that the bar caused when taking photos and videos..
Considerations:
A truly very interesting tour, however during the booking phase, as is done with all commercial flights, the possibility of choosing seats should be given, possibly also offering differentiated prices because whoever is in front or without any annoying impediment is certainly very advantaged.
Furthermore, if there are two of you, it seems really mean to me to put both of you in the worst places!!
In my opinion Air Ventures should care more about customer satisfaction, which, unfortunately, they don't.

Review Text:
This may very well be the most beautiful place I have ever visited. We were in Oahu for one week and then Kauai. Why did we not just go to Kauai for two weeks?
We had a small condo in Kapaa in the Coconut Beach area and that is where we will stay when we come again. I like the area and it is pretty easy to get everywhere from there. There is a park nearby called Lydgate Park that would be great to take kids to or anyone leery of ocean swimming as it has 2 areas blocked off by big boulders so that there is no worry about getting in too deep or being knocked down by waves. It also has a huge playground.
We initially were holding a very expensive rental car but I kept checking and got it down to a reasonable amount. There is no charge to park anywhere we went.
Be prepared for bad roads if you go the scenic route. Many of the scenic roads are rutted and have potholes the size of a VW bug. When it rains on Kauai (it rains a lot), there are red mud puddles in areas that you will go to sightsee. If you plan to hike, take it seriously. Many of the hikes are considered to be for those more experienced hikers and you will need real hiking shoes. Also plan on slippery areas on the hike so a fall in the mud is possible.
The rest of the island has good roads and no mud so you don’t have to engage with the mud if you don’t want to.
We paid for an app called the Shaka guide. They offer 4 GPS tours which covers the whole island and is definitely worth the money!
This island has a slower pace than Oahu but you can still get into traffic in the morning and evening drive time if you are around Lihue.
The airport is adorable and very easy to get around. Don’t be surprised to find chickens near the luggage carousel. i read that Kauai has about 75,000 people and 450,000 chickens. Therefore don’t expect to sleep much past sunrise due to the roosters crowing. But then who would want to miss a sunrise in Kauai anyway?

Review Title: Amazing Value & Great Tour Guide - Justin
Review Text:
Booked Air Ventures Hawaii on Kauai for a same week excursion. We found them on Tinggly and saw their reviews on that site before booking. It was an amazing decision! I have been on a Kauai helicopter ride as well so I was able to experience both.

Air Ventures is definitely a value for the experience! Our pilot Justin was considerate and caring. He answered all my questions about the island and really made an effort to show the best of the island including pointing out a humpback whale off the Nepali coast!

A few notes on the services itself:
- $149 per person is a deal!
- The right side of the plane sees more of the best of the island including waterfalls and the Napali coast, but Justin did an amazing job making sure the left side got to see everything too with some awesome turns.
- The plane is not like a doors off helicopter. It's a smoother ride, and the views are less dramatic. For those who are prone to air sickness, I highly recommend over the helicopter.
- Parking and check-in is a breeze, it's right by the FedEx and has a designated parking lot
- Very organized operations and the staff are super friendly

I would highly recommend Air Ventures Hawaii in Kauai!

The tour office was a quick and easy walk from the main Kauai airport in Lihue—this was especially nice for us, as we were just over to Kauai on a day trip from Maui and didn’t have a rental car! This was a really great tour and a really good way to see the Na Pali Coastline and the canyons within the island without having to go by boat. I’m prone to sea sickness, so this was a perfect solution for me. Isaac was very knowledgeable and friendly and we felt very safe in his care. We were seated in the middle seats, unfortunately, so we had our views partially obstructed by the wings, so our views and photos weren’t great. I guess someone has to sit there, but for future flyers, try for the backseat or the front with the pilot for the best views!

It was a real treat because the private flight should have been more like $700 instead of the $300 we paid for a one hour flight,

Our pilots name was Bud, I think? He was a young guy, with only a few years flying experience. I think I soloed before he was even born? He was building hours and hoping to get hired by Hawaiian Airmon the Airbus 320Neo. I wish him the best of luck because 20 years ago that was my plan to for their lines. Plans changed though.

It was an amazing flight. Haven’t flown in a small Cessna for over twenty years. It was great to get back in the air in a small GA plane.

We were able to see the entire island, and Nate took care to operate the airplane with smoothness and an aim to provide views to all passengers. He delivered on that and more. Nate was able answer all of our questions and we learned about Kauai, the land, the sea, the rivers, the mountains, and the people. Very knowledgeable! The views that Air Ventures Hawaii provides are as good or perhaps much better than a helicopter tour at a great value for a family. I would give Air Ventures Hawaii my strongest recommendation.
I am serving customers every day in my job, and I know the many challenges one can encounter when trying to deliver your best service. Review Text:
I was on the island of Oahu, Hawaii when my plans to visit Pearl Harbor fell through.  I didn’t want to waste one day of our two week vacation and so I decided to research how I could visit Kauai for one day. You may think that is a ridiculous idea however, once I found Air Ventures Hawaii and spoke to a representative early Wednesday morning to secure the proper flight times for Thursday I decided to book a flight to Lihue via Southwest.  We arrived at noon and our Air Ventures flight was booked for 1:30pm.  The cost was $337.08 (two passengers) for one hour.  This flight was definitely longer, less expensive, and more beautiful than our helicopter tour that we took a few days prior to this adventure.  Trisha and her assistant greeted us with a warm Aloha and they were extremely professional and helpful.  I am happy that they informed us about paying $30.00 to capture the GoPro footage of our one hour flight.  The footage from the NaPali Coast was unbelievable yet stunning! It is well worth the money.  
Prior to boarding we were weighed and seated in a nice open air waiting room.  I would suggest that a few hours prior to the flight that you take Dramamine to ensure you will not experience any motion sickness.  I always practiced this so I didn’t have any problems on the flight.  I believe only one passenger was somewhat ill.  I think this is important because the flight is absolutely breathtaking and you simply don’t want to be ill while enjoying such an unimaginable view.  Please be mindful that Air Ventures Hawaii has no control over Mother Nature and sometimes a few bumps might occur throughout the flight.  
Nate was our pilot. I must admit that this guy was stellar!!!  First, he has the best personality.  He welcomed us aboard as guests, explained all safety precautions, told us exactly what would happen while in flight, and even explained what we would see while on the trip.  In addition, he was a skilled aviator that paid attention to the details of safety and also provided valuable information at the same time.  I am very happy that Air Ventures Hawaii takes passenger safety seriously.  
In addition to being a good aviator the pilot did an excellent job of explaining all the different sights that we saw during the flight.  I must admit that I love seeing the Grand Canyon of the Pacific and the waterfalls however, the NaPali Coast is a sight to behold.  Nate indicated that the NaPali Coast is considered one of the most beautiful coastlines in the world.  I agree with him unequivocally!! My eyes have not seen such natural uninhabited beauty like that since visiting Bora Bora in 2007.  The beauty of the NaPali Coast is the best reason to take this flight.  In addition, if you can only spend a day on the island it will take two hours to reach the NaPali Coast and I believe much of it cannot be reached by foot.  I believe seeing the coastline from the air is unexplainable in words and unimaginable even when you see it.  Bucket list for sure!!!!!

Air ventures is a great way to do this activity. The plane ride is much more keenly priced than the helicopters, and I venture (no pun intended) to suggest just as good.

I strongly recommend AirVentures to anyone eager to see and learn about Kaua’i.

Review Text:
Vielleicht ist es wichtig zu sagen, dass viele der atemberaubenden Landschaften auf Kauai lediglich per Boot oder gar nicht zugänglich sind. Das erklärt, warum Kauai so paradiesisch ist… Denn hier kann die Natur in freien Bahnen wachsen und gedeihen.

Da ich (fast) alleine reiste und beim besten Willen nicht alles zu Fuß oder Auto hätte sehen können, entschied ich mich für diese Tour.

Allen Liebhaber außergewöhnlicher Landschaften und der Natur insgesamt kann ich diesen Flug nur empfehlen. Hier ein paar Punkte, die mir wichtig waren und erfüllt bzw. übertroffen wurden:

TOUR: In der Tat handelt es sich um eine KOMPLETTE Tour. Wir umrundeten die Insel und haben alles gesehen, was in jedem Reiseführer empfohlen wird (wahrscheinlich) auch noch mehr.

FÜR ALLE: da ich allein war, durfte ich mich auf Nachfrage einfach neben den Piloten hinsetzen. Was natürlich mega war. Besonders charmant fand ich, dass der Pilot immer gedreht hat, damit nicht nur die Passagieren an der rechten sondern auch an der linken Seite alles sehen konnten.
Das habe ich selten bei vorherigen Rundflügen erlebt.

SICHERHEIT: Von der Buchung bis zur Durchführung hatte ich stets den Eindruck, dass das gesamte Personal an alles gedacht hat. Die Machine war sauber und flog problemlos, der Pilot hatte neben den üblichen Elementen auch ein iPad am Board und ging damit und mit dem Flugzeit selbstverständlich um.
Bevor wir einstiegen wurde unseren Impf/Teststatus erneut geprüft.

PILOT: Unser Pilot Nate ist extrem erfahren, ortskundig und sehr professionell. Die Kombi hat es möglich gemacht, dass er neben der kurzen und verständlichen Erklärungen auch Zeit für Witze gefunden hat.

PREIS-LEISTUNGSVERHÄLTNIS: Einfach Top. Wer schon mal in Deutschland einen Rundflug gemacht hat, weißt, dass 30-45 Minuten schon mal 170€ kosten können.
Für 130€ haben wir die ganze Insel gesehen, super Erklärungen und Insights bekommen, waren über 70 Minuten in der Luft und hatten eine butterweiche Landung. Mehr geht echt nicht.

Die Krönung für mich war, dass ich danach gefragt habe, ob Jill (die super nette Amerikanerin an der Rezeption für mich ein Taxi rufen konnte). Nach ein paar Minuten kam Jill mit Ray (einem anderen Piloten), der mich gefragt hat, ob er mich zum Hotel fahren dürfte, da er 3 Stunden bis zur nächsten Tour frei hat. Ist das nicht traumhaft??? :)
Ray war über 40 Jahre Pilot bei einer amerikanischen Airline und setzte sich mit seiner Frau vor 20 Jahren hier ab. Es war super nett, bei ihm mitfahren zu dürfen und so viele coole Geschichten zu hören!

Es war tatsächlich der schönste Rundflug, den ich in meinem Leben gemacht habe.

Und für diesen Paradies würde ich die Tour als ein MUSS empfehlen.

Review Title: Enjoying the Majesty and Beauty of The Island of Kauai
Review Text:
This is my second time taking the Island Air Tour; this time we brought friends with us. To say that we had a memorable experience is an understatement. The scenery from the air was breathtaking; everything from the Poipu Coast, Waimea Canyon, the amazing waterfalls, Hanalei Bay and the Islands beauty. My favorite remains the Napali Coastline in all it's magnificent splendor; it truly is Bali Hai.

Ten years ago we flew with Ray Smith, a 34 year veteran flying Jumbo Jets for United Airlines. Since then, Ray bought the company and still loves sharing this beautiful Island with all his guest. Our pilot today was Nate who was not only friendly but very knowledgeable in sharing with us so much about Kauai that we had never heard on any other tour during our several visits to Kauai. Nate also was more than willing to fly back over parts of the Island that we wanted to see up close again. Even though this is the middle of November with unpredictable weather we had beautiful sunshine and even the highest point on Kauai was fully visible.

The plane itself is unique, built in Australia to use by Bush pilots, the aircraft is steady and able to cruise much slower than the Helicopters that you can tour with on the Island. The interior of the aircraft was comfortable even for me who is 6'1" and 230 lbs. In fact I got to sit in the Co-Pilots seat! Each seat however has a bubble window which gives excellent visibility and is perfect for your camera or I phone for picture taking. Every guest has a headphone which keeps you in contact with the pilot and all the other guest. The headphones also filter out excess engine noise which enables everyone to carry on a pleasant conversation and to ask any question they wish about the Island.

Ray and his wife are truly customer oriented in answering questions and making this a great experience from beginning to end.

We love coming to Kauai to go swimming on the amazing beaches; riding bicycles; go on Snorkeling and Dinner Cruises; tubing in the sugar cane canals; and of course the Luaus. All of these are fun and have produced lasting memories with our children and now our grandchildren. Having done all of this over the years I can honestly say, If there is only 1 tour that you must take on Kauai, Air Adventures is that tour.

I was able to mount my GoPro on the outside of the plane (for a small fee) and got some great footage of the Napali coast and other areas. The staff was experienced with handling GoPro's and got it all set up nicely for me as I was a new user.
Everyone raves about the helicopter tours but I would say that the private Cessna tour is another thing not to be missed, both for the views and for the personal, fun experience with this amazing company.

Review Text:
We had the open cockpit biplane flight beginning of February after booking online from the UK. Jill kindly offered to collect/shuttle us from the ABC Store at Anchor Cove Shopping Mall which is very close to the Cruise terminal. She gave us a scenic ride to the airport via some scenic gardens which was unexpected. The small office was very friendly and efficient with space for bulky belongings.
There we met Kevin, our pilot who immediately put Jane's mind at ease as she was very apprehensive of small aircraft and open cockpit. He assured her that the flight would have no 'aerobatics', just relax & enjoy it. An extra cushion was provided so as to help look out.
After putting on a vintage style cloth helmet with noise cancelling earphones we were ready for take off. It was warm in the cockpit, just a tee shirt is enough even in February as you have the radial engine just forward of your feet. We flew a circle over the cruise ship and all the way down the westerly coast including the spectacular Na-Pali coastline overflying white surf and coral reefs. Turning inland the Waimea Canyon was laid out beneath us on our return to the airport. Kevin gave a superb commentary. A big advantage of the open cockpit was that you don't get window reflections in your photographs - or having to look through scratched or milky plexiglass.
80% of Kauai is inaccessible so the only way to appreciate its majesty is from the air on this 65 minute flight. We hired a car for the rest of the day and drove to the end of the Canyon road as well - not much to see from the tree lined road so you would need to walk the trails so glad we had the flight.
On our return we were also shuttled to the Avis car depot.
At first sight the trip sounded expensive at 500USD (£390) for us both but for the experience of a vintage style aircraft in such an exotic place it most definitely was not. Putting it in perspective, the previous day we paid 300USD for us to have a minibus sightseeing excursion on Big Island. No contest!!
To those hesitant of the aircraft - don't be. Open cockpit is exhilarating and all that fresh air and immersion in the experience blows away any concerns of nausia. Jane was Cock-a Hoot afterwards with absolutely no regrets.
We are very well travelled seniors and this flight is surely one of our highlights.

Review Text:
I knew without a doubt that I wanted to take an airplane tour over the island. We selected Air Ventura after reading reviews. Found a great coupon on a discount Hawaii website.
They ask you to arrive 30 minutes prior to departure. When we made the reservation they asked our weights, then weighed us and any baggage we were carrying upon arrival. So, don’t lie.
We were walked out to he plane with a couple who was on our flight. We all took some photos with the pilot and plane. We were then given assigned seats. Don’t assume that you will be sitting with your party. I’m assuming they are managing a combination of weight disruption and how comfortable they think people will be in different seats. There is a co pilot space - which is great for someone older or who has mobility issues. The next two seats are probably the most squished. The third row is just one seat. There is a little aisle room to stretch your left leg out. There are two seats in the back. It is a very tight squeeze height wise getting in. I am not a small person and I fit okay in the sets and was able to buckle without problems.
They provide a cooler full of water and also cold, wet towels. Although they try to keep the cabin cool I was definitely a little warm
by the end. That combined with the banking turns and a few bumps had me
not feeling 100%. The cool towel on the back of my neck had me feeling better right away.
Our pilot, TJ, was knowledgeable and personable. He kept us well informed of the flying conditions we would have as well as what we were seeing. I like how he doubled back several times to get us some great views.
The scenery is so varied on the island. I could have done with a little less of the towns and a few minute shorter flight, but it was fantastic. I enjoyed flying over the coffee plantation at Kauai Coffee. Nepali Coast was gorgeous. The canyons were incredible. Hands down though, the highlight for me was the Cathedrals. They were stunning.
Well run operation. Very clean planes. You can tell they take a lot of pride in their fleet.
There are lots of beautiful parts of the island you’ll never see if you don’t do it by air. Would definitely recommend Air Ventures. And, don’t forget to tip your pilot!

Review Text:
Truly outstanding airplane ride on one of the loveliest places on earth. I'm a long-time pilot but somehow never managed to ride in a bi-plane, so it was a dream come true for me to finally get to ride in one (now if only I could have flown it too! ;)

There are lots of ways you can see Kauai by air. None are cheap. But every other method has you watching out a window like it's TV screen. Take this trip and you directly experience the island with all your senses, you're not just a passive viewer.

Our pilot Kevin has been doing this a long time and clearly loves his job. With so many movies filmed here and so few pilots over the years available, Kevin has had a lot of fun experiences working with film crews and actors over the years and has plenty of fun stories to tell during the flight, in addition to the standard descriptions of the sights,

If you are wondering how safe the trip is, then as a pilot I can tell you that you are in very good hands with this outfit. The plane is obviously extremely well cared for (and loved!) and in excellent condition, the pilot is very safety-conscious, and he isn't a show-off that puts you in danger. This is a solid operator that knows how to do it right, you are in good hands here.

And if you worry about the open-cockpit aspect: you'll have a cloth helmet and goggles, and you are actually not really in the airstream unless you go out of your way to get into it while peering over the side to something down below. With the wing above you for shade, no worries about getting too much sun, and the air is not cold. It's actually a really pleasant experience in the open cockpit that you will really like!

Bottom line: truly unique experience for one or two passengers, from a very safe outfit who knows what they are doing. There simply isn't a better flying experience on the island.

Review Title: How to Experience Kauai via Air
Review Text:
When you pick an aerial solution to fly over Kauai, you have basically two choices - helicopters or fixed wing aircraft.

Air ventures represents the best solution on Kauai for the fixed wing option.

We chose to take the 8:30 AM tour, on our first day after we arrived on Kauai. While it would seem somewhat early in the AM to rally the troops after getting to the island, the 8:30 AM flight worked well, from the time adjustment perspective. Winds in the early AM are somewhat calmer, and temperatures cooler than later flights.

We were able to grab a light breakfast prior to heading to the airport @ 8AM for our flight.

This aerial solution offers a great overview perspective of Kauai from a 1000-3000 ft perspective, permitting great photographs, a more stable platform, with more visibility for each person, with oversized window seats, at a reasonable price structure.

Everyone has a full window seat in an “air van” like setting, with noise cancelling headphones to communicate with the others, or the pilot. We chose the 6 passenger option, however, smaller two - three seat aircraft options are available.

Make no mistake, we saw a lot of helicopters flying at lower altitudes, however, the fixed wing perspective offers fuller vistas, and covers similar territory over a longer flight experience. For our group, this worked best...as weight restrictions are more lenient in a fixed wing aircraft, and air sickness concerns were a consideration in our choice.

We saw a lot of the island from Napali Coast, many of the interior canyons; the vibrant blues of the ocean, sea turtles, and dolphins; several waterfalls, Hanalei and Princeville areas. From our group, this provided the overall perspective and island layout we were looking for.

By going with Air Ventures, we saved several hundred dollars from a comparable flight alternative via helicopter.

We highly recommend this alternative to see Kauai by air. This was our second tour with Air Ventures Hawaii.

Pilot, Erik, was very knowledgeable, professional, experienced in a relaxing manner that permitted the others he travelled with to also feel more comfortable.

Review Text:
Short version: amateur, unprofessional, overpriced, uncomfortable, rude, terrible experience. Spend the extra money and take a he'll ride, or at least use a different plane ride provider!

Long version: We arrived at 925 for our 10am departure, and after the counter employees spent ten minutes in what seemed like some kind of candid camera routine, they informed us that there was some kind of "system error" leaving us as the only two passengers for the flight, which they "couldn't do." They told us we had to come back at 11.
We returned at 11 and waited over an hour before we finally got in the air with a pilot who clearly had very little experience flying or in customer service. After informing us he "wasn't supposed to be here today" and that the pilots don't even get paid, and that one of these tour planes had just crash landed the other day, we proceeded on our unprofessional and abbreviated tour of the island. After learning we were newlyweds he informed us that he was thinking of getting engaged so he could stop using condoms but that he had been a man whose so his girl wamts him to use them. This was one of the few statements he made that didn't begin with "I'm not supposed to tell you this, but..."
I know that they cannot be held accountable for inclement weather but we deliberately booked the earliest flight available to get out before the weather turned. About the time the 10am flight landed the storm moved in and we were unable to see much of anything on our flight.

Had we been on the flight we booked (both airbusses flew at 10am, despite the story that there were only two of us booked) we might have an entirely different review.
Had they just admitted it was their mistake we might have an entirely different review.
Had they just been honest before takeoff that due to weather we would not be able to see the napali coast, we might have an entirely different review.

But the unprofessional pilot and the unprofessional gate staff and the unprofessional business model of this place left us wishing we had spent the extra money and taken a helicopter ride instead of what now feels like a tourist trap rip-off. Cannot even shrug this off as a "you get what you pay for" experience, as we paid for a 10am professionally piloted all-island tour. And got a short plane ride with a kid who didn't want to be there, and frankly, shouldn't have.

Review Text:
We did this Tour on May 21st 2019. Initially, I was looking for helicopter tours but on discovering that they assign seats based on height and weight and that the helicopter has “middle seats” I decided to look into Air ventures. I am glad I did.
First off, there are no middle seats; everyone gets a window. I had booked the morning tour, but due to unforeseen circumstances, the tour had to be moved to the afternoon. They were kind enough to inform me 1 day before the trip. The change was done free of charge. If we could not make it, they were willing to rebook us on a different day that would work out. If we could not attend, I am sure they would have refunded us.
We had 4 people in total who took the same plane ride with us, so we all sat on the same side, but had there been more our pilot Justin T (not Timberlake! ) would have maneuvered the plane so all could get a good look.
The view of the NaPali coast from air was breathtaking. Justin also played some mild background music while he narrated the history of Kauai and pointed out interesting features. For me seeing the NaPali coast and the beautiful reefs from the sky was like the scene from Avatar where the protagonist sees the Floating Mountains of Pandora for the first time. Magnificent. We also saw the Waimea canyon (also known as Grand Canyon of the Pacific). It was lush green and had countless waterfalls. Justin was kind enough to fly the plane around slowly and more than once so we could truly take in the beauty. I was lucky enough to get to sit in the co-pilot’s seat, but all the seats are good. Do make sure you wear all black clothes, else your reflection will show up in the window and ruin your photos. The windows are large enough that you get a good view and squeaky clean too. Review Title: Beautiful Island, Beautiful Airplane, Great Tour!
Review Text:
As a pilot, I heard about Air Ventures from another pilot friend and made my plan based on that recommendation. This was definitely the way to go. Call them direct and make the reservation vs. the web site. You can get all the details and work out the best time and expected best local conditions (there is always some kind of cloud activity on every island's mountains).
They offer several ways to tour the island but there was no doubt I wanted to go in the Cessna 182 (they may call it luxury tour but for a few bucks extra you get the plane to yourselves and can get personal with your pilot). I own my own plane and have been flying for 30 years, but this was the nicest Cessna 182 I have ever been in. Fully equipped with G1000s, Bose noise cancelling A20 headsets(the best there are), and even an air-conditioner. My pilot was Eric Johnson, a CFI with 8000 hours of flight time. Really fun guy and exceptional pilot. I knew right from the start I had picked the right company, plane, & pilot.
We circled the island as well as flew up thru the mountain passes enjoying the scenery and waterfalls. Way better than in a helicopter or the C208 caravan.
My wife is used to flying with me, but Eric went out of his way to make sure she was comfortable and enjoying the view. I've flown with lots of pilots and CFIs over the years and it is a rare breed that can be fun, informative, highly competent, and safe at all times.
All in all a really fun and informative flight experience I would recommend to all.

Pilot seat up front , I sat behind the pilot . Finally when we landed the person at the front desk gave me ginger ale to drink. I will say it took a few days to get feeling back

This was a jaw dropping experience. I debated doing a plane ride vs a helicopter, then once I decided on a plane ride there were a lot of companies to choose from. Then after reading many strong and positive reviews about Air Ventures, I booked with them. I chose well! One of the things that sold me on this company was that there are no middle seats, so everyone gets a window.
The flight did travel in a clockwise direction, so seats on the right hand side were preferable. The pilot did circle around at some sites so that everyone could get a clear view, but there was a definite advantage to being on the right hand side of the plane.
The pilot gave great commentary and let us know what sites we were flying over, and he was happy to answer any questions that we had.
The planes can't get as close to some of the sites as a helicopter (such as Jurassic Falls), but this was a non issue based on the amazing experience we had.
Overall, this was one of the highlights of my time on Kauai. It was a really great way to see the island. We were there on a clear day with smooth air, so it made it even better!

Review Text:
Aside from the opportunity to soak in some gorgeous and dramatic views of the island, the whole-island tour was an especially enjoyable trip for a pilot. I had originally wanted to fly in their C182, a private 4-seat Cessna, with an instructor, because it is the only way to fly around the island, at the controls, unless you take a checkout flight so you can rent further, solo (more of an option for residents). My wife and I decided this time to take the tour in the AirVan, with J.T. as our pilot and tour guide, along with a few other passengers.

Even though we pilots are always itching to be at the controls, this was still a fine choice. The airspace is relatively busy with other air tours and traffic, there are several local VFR reference points you don’t know, and the terrain has unique properties which require attention, as well. I was simply able to sit back and enjoy the beauty of Kauai—without getting too antsy to fly, myself!

Incidentally, with the varying terrain and ocean comes what’s called “uneven heating” which is one of the factors which creates turbulence. There’s only two things one can do to mitigate that: 1) fly early in the morning, or 2) get a pilot who knows how to soften the ride (there are a few ways). J.T. is just such a pilot.

Highly recommend! (20 year, instrument pilot)

Review Text: Last Wednesday on a day with a few highish clouds we flew on a tour with Air Ventures of Kaua'i, the most westerly of the tourist-visited Hawaiian islands.  Unlike the standard helicopter tour that last 45 minutes and can be a rushed experience, this trip in a fixed wing aircraft was over an hour in duration, allowing for a more leisured experience, with time for whale watching as well as a more detailed look at the south of the island and the famous Na Pali coast on the North West. Everyone gets a window seat, making for easier photography sith reduced distortion from the curved surfaces typical of helicopter windows.  All-in-all at US165$ each, this experience was excellent value and we will be choosing this option in the future.

Review Text:
We recently took an Air Ventures tour circling the island of Kauai...what an incredible experience!!! The plane has oversized windows and holds just 6 passengers, so it seemed like a private tour. One fortunate passenger (Laura below) was even able to sit in the co-pilot seat for the entire flight!

Our pilot T.J. was wonderful (and funny) and interactive, describing what we were seeing along the way. He even spotted some whales and circled them twice to make sure we had an incredible view. In addition, two of our fellow passengers had arrived by passenger ship, so T.J. made sure to fly over the ship on our return to the airport...it was very, very cool!

In addition to T.J., everyone we came into contact with from Air Ventures was great...starting with the young lady who took our reservation over the phone, kept us updated on the status of the flight, and greeted us when we arrived. What is very special about Air Ventures is that it is a family owned and run local business. We know this because we were assisted by Jill, a co-owner, who couldn't have been more kind and helpful. After our flight she even returned us to our hotel (Kauai Marriott Resort) instead of us getting a taxi or Uber.

This was our final adventure before heading back to the mainland and it was the perfect way to conclude our trip.

Thank you Air Ventures!!!

Laura Overcash
Hank Kirschenmann
Alexandria, VA

Review Title: Verborgen Schat met de beste Kauai ervaring ooit!
Review Text:
Omdat wij een Cruise hadden geboekt langs de eilanden van Hawaï en het excursie aanbod vanuit de rederij niet echt aantrekkelijk was, ben ik verder gaan zoeken en kwam ik via TripAdvisor en de touristenpagina van Hawaï beoordelingen tegen van Air Ventures.
Direct viel me op dat ze prijstechnisch enorm voordelig waren ten opzichte van de overdaad aan andere chartermaatschappijen, wat me in eerste instantie wel deed twijfelen. Het leek immers mooier dan waar te zijn.
Op de website staan de diverse mogelijkheden die aangeboden worden. Zo kun je een gedeeld vliegtuigje nemen, bieden ze een privé optie aan en hebben ze ook een ouderwets propellervliegtuig met open cockpit voor een nog exclusievere ervaring.
In tegenstelling tot andere maatschappijen werken ze niet met helicopters, maar met kleine vliegtuigen waar max 6 gasten aan boord kunnen en iedereen een eigen raam heeft om van te genieten.
Je kunt gemakkelijk online boeken en de agenda inzien. Ook kun je ze vlak van tevoren bellen om te vragen of ze nog beschikbaarheid hebben.
Betalen kan online of aan de balie ter plaatse.
De medewerkers zijn zeer vriendelijk en behulpzaam en de reactietijd is fantastisch.
Ik had vooraf een vraag over hun optie om mijn eigen GoPro aan de buitenzijde van het vliegtuig te laten bevestigen, waar ik snel een reactie op kreeg en ter plaatse overigens ook zeer goed bij geassisteerd ben.
Eenmaal op de dag van vertrek was het zeer bewolkt en regenachtig. Op de afgesproken ophaallocatie werden we onthaald door een medewerker van Air Ventures die vertelde dat de vlucht niet veilig was en geen doorgang kon vinden. We kregen direct de optie aangeboden om iets later die dag het opnieuw te proberen en indien dat niet mogelijk was wegens weersomstandigheden, we ons geld geretourneerd zouden krijgen. Zij wilden ons immers ook de beste ervaring kunnen bieden.
Ten tijde van onze tweede poging begon het langzaam beter weer te worden, dus konden we alsnog naar het vliegveld. Daar werd kort een instructie gegeven over wat te verwachten en werd de plaatsindeling door de piloot gedaan, die rekening hield met de fotografen onder de groep.
Mijn GoPro werd bevestigd aan de buitenzijde van het vliegtuig en werd samen gecontroleerd of de positie goed was en er verbinding gemaakt kon worden via de app.
Omdat het zo had geregend waren we gezegend met talloze watervallen gedurende de vlucht.
We zijn vrijwel het hele eiland over geweest en werden gedurende de vlucht van informatie voorzien door onze grappige piloot, die er echt een feestje van maakte. We hebben zelfs nog even kort in formatie gevlogen met een ander vliegtuig van Air Ventures, wat echt een unieke ervaring was.
Al met al denk ik dat wij het meeste hebben gezien van alle mensen aan boord, gezien de dag ervoor ook alles al volledig betrokken was, terwijl we met deze vlucht zowel de Waimea Canyon als de Napali Coast hebben gezien.
Mocht je voor korte (of lange) duur op Kauai zijn, is dit ABSOLUUT een aanrader en de nummer 1 tour om te boeken. Maar niet te veel doorvertellen hoor, anders zitten ze voor het hele jaar volgeboekt. ;-)

Review Title: Great pilot, bad judgement on the part of the owner
Review Text: We took this air tour around Kauai in late September. The weather in Kauai is often very unstable, and it was particularly so while we were there. It was pouring rain across the entire island the morning of the day we took our air tour, but when I called Air Ventures to make a reservation for two days later, there was a break in the weather. The owner (at least I believe he was the owner) told me that the conditions were great if I wanted to go that day, and that he could book me for that afternoon, so I did. When we arrived, we were told that all flights had been canceled that day because of bad weather but they were still hoping to get out that afternoon. We took off on schedule, and it was a beautiful tour, but Waimea canyon was completely socked in and we couldn't see it at all, and there were lots of clouds to contend with along the entire flight. I felt that we had been misled about the conditions that day, and if I had known that the weather would be so unstable I wouldn't have booked the trip. Also, if I did it again I'd go in a helicopter. We saw helicopters touring the canyon and the coast later during our stay and they could get much closer to the sights and provide better views. Still, the pilot was great and overall it was a good experience. But I was terribly disappointed at not seeing the canyon.

Review Text:
Our photography flight with Air Ventures—the most eco-friendly air tour company in Kauai—was one of the highlights of our Hawaiian adventure. Owner Jill Briley and her outgoing staff ensured that everything was air-tight prior to takeoff. With over 8,000 hours of flight time and a sparkling personality, Captain Eric ensured that we were safe and entertained from takeoff to landing.

Soaring over Kauai was a truly amazing experience. We covered a lot of ground from the air—the entire Garden Island—in just over an hour with the Big Kahuna tour.

The most epic highlights on an island of breathtaking coastlines were Waita Reservoir (the largest on Kauai), Captain Cook’s Landing, the inspiring Waimea Canyon, the surreal Napali Coastline, Lumahai Beach (where “South Pacific” was filmed), Hanalei Valley, countless beautiful cascading waterfalls and the Kilauea Lighthouse. It is so beautiful that over 60 movies have been filmed here, including Blue Hawaii, King Kong, Jurassic Park, Soul Surfer, The Descendants and Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides.

Review Text:
I had never been in a small craft before, so I was scared and relictant even as I buckled in while still on the tarmac. Even after the smooth take-off, and cruise past landmarks, I still expected the plane to buck and pitch and to cause me to use the air-sickness bag. However, none of the former or latter happened. Our pilot, Eric, with his 30 years of flying expertise, flew that plane rock steady. His calm demeanor, seemingly effortless flying, and his abundant knowledge of the island distracted my mind from my unfounded fears of a plane-crash death.
As for the sights, we were able to see most of the must-see places all over the island. The views were so good in fact, that we didn’t even feel the need to see them up close anymore. Why go to the (Fantasy Island) waterfalls by car just to see it from the freeway, when we’ve already seen it from the best angle available? The same went for spouting horn and other attractions. We even saw sea turtles from our vantage point in the air.
But what goes up must come down. Again, Captain Eric did not disappoint. The landing was so smooth I didn’t even feel the moment when the wheels actually touched the ground.
All in all a great flight. I highly recommend it!!

Review Text: We had a great flight in "Woodstock", the bright yellow biplane that Kevin flies. First he gave us a little background about the plane, then a cockpit tour, then pictures with the plane, and then we loaded up and took off. Two people sit side by side in the cockpit right behind the motor, with the pilot in the back. Head gear with headphones are provided so you can talk back and forth to the pilot (all you need to complete the outfit is a scarf). Also because you're sitting right behind the motor there's no need for a jacket. Kevin has been on the island for about 30 years, so he can describe all the sites you fly over, and give you a great history and geography lesson at the same time. It's not a great flight to take if you want a ton of pictures because it's hard to get the camera at the right angle because of the placement of the wings, but instead, just ride along and enjoy the view. We had a blast! At the end of the flight we had our picture taken in the plane, so we have something to prove we were real aviators for a day. All the staff were very friendly and Kevin was a very competent pilot. We highly recommend this tour.

Review Text:
Excellent tour guide/pilot. I believe his name was Kevin, guy with the mustache.

The flight was excellent. We go to see the majority of the key point of the island.
It was much more affordable then a helicopter and I believe it gave you a more stable view to take pictures and videos!

From take off, to landing everything was smooth.
It did get a little hot at one point, but they provide cool towels if you get to hot, so I'd recommend just wearing shorts and t-shirt. No long sleeves or jackets are needed.

The weather was great, so we got to see just about everything we wanted to, with clear skies!

The only tiny issue we encounter was understanding where to park and where we'd have to go to board the plane. We've never flown a private plane before, so we figured i'd be similar to a comercial plane, where we'd have to park in a large lot and go through TSA screening etc.... Maybe these instructions are provided if you book directly, we booked through hawaii discounts. Rest assured, its quick and painless process, you literally go to their address, you park right at the parking lot outside of their offices, you walk into their offices, which is right on tarmac, check in and they'll walk you on to the plane.

It was an excellent flight, affordable, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone.

Highlights included Poipu beach, Waimea Canyon and the Princeville area before flying cross country over the jungle back to Lihue Airport.

The best part of the trip was flying out over the Niipali coast, and watching humpback whales breaching the surface and splashing back down. The pilot, who was excellent through the whole trip, circled around three or four times to let us watch the whales play.

Everybody should do this trip.

Review Text:
We were very fortunate to choose Air Ventures for our flight over Kauai. Choosing such an early morning flight and being a couple gave us a special surprise when we arrived - we were able to fly in the new 4 seater Cesna! Very comfortable and smooth flight, plus the great headphones made our pilots commentary clear and easy to enjoy.

The flight path sights were brilliant and really gave us a great perspective of the area we had covered earlier the week by car and foot. Our pilot really ensured we saw as much as possible. Of course the Napali Coast line was spectacular. To top the experience off the early morning light rain followed by morning low sunshine meant at the northern tip of the Napali Coast flying over the water with the sun low behind us a full circular rainbow was suspended below us. Our pilot jokingly told us to look below and find the end of the rainbow which of course to our amazement didn't exist. He flew around its huge circumference and I wished there had been an under aircraft mounted camera on the plane to have captured it's breathtaking beauty - my camera just couldn't take it all in!
Our flight was fabulous, the staff friendly and professional and such good value for money.
If you are looking for an air experience in Kauai I would definitely contact Air Ventures!

I hope to return to Kawai in 6 months At which time I plan to take the bi plane tour With Air Ventures Hawaii.
My trip to Kauai was my fulfillment of a dream to return to Hawaii after having been in the military in the Hawaiian Island chain 40 plus years ago. My trip began on Veterans day and i enjoyed my 63rd birthday on Kauai. My 10 day trip to Kawaii involved the drive up Wiamea Canyon, The fixed wing flight over and around the island and a 5 hour kayak tour up the Royal river with a one hour hike into the rain forest to The Secret waterfall. I can only hope the reader will experience the island energy AND the island love from both Thee Island And Her prople the way I did. Again, much about my experience began with the fixed wing flight over and around the island with Air Adventures Hawaii. Yes I will do it again...in rhe bi plane next time....
Aloha and mahalo.

Air Ventures even picked us up from our hotel and dropped us back as we were staying fairly close by but didn't have a car. Friendly, efficient team and pilot and everything went smoothly. Strongly suggest you take their advice and wear a dark top to cut down reflections. Loved the waterfalls, Na Pali coast, farms - everything. So don't be hesitant, book and you will be like and so glad I did.

Happy memories and the best tour ever, thanks to Eric, Jill and grand staff.

Review Title: Great pilot, friendly ground crew, amazing service!
Review Text:
We had originally booked the Vintage Bi-Plane tour and were really excited for it, but were contacted by AirVentures shortly before our trip to let us know that there had been an incident on the tarmac (not AirVentures fault) and their bi-plane had been unfortunately damaged. Given their commitment to safety, they were cancelling all bi-plane tours until they could arrange for a new plane. All changes to our plans were handled very professionally and AirVentures did everything in their power to make sure our tour was fantastic and fit into our plans given the rescheduling!

I actually got to ride in the co-pilot's seat (which was amazing!) and we enjoyed one of the best tours of our entire trip. It had rained heavily for two or three days straight so it seemed that every waterfall on the island was running heavily, which was a real treat to see. The pilot was friendly and offered very interesting commentary throughout the flight. Takeoff and landing were both smooth and we would do the tour again in a heartbeat - so beautiful!

We had a lot to do before making it back to our terminal with enough time left to check-in, etc.   The staff at Air Ventures understood our situation so while my parents were up in the air taking their tour, one of the gentleman on their staff offered to drive me to the rental hub to return our rental vehicle. Review Text:
Wir wollten einen Rundflug über Kaua‘i machen also stellte sich die Frage wie??

Vorteil von Helikopter ist das man nah an die Attraktionen fliegt, das ist dann aber schon der einzige.

Vorteile vom Flugzeug, jeder hat seinen eigenen Fensterplatz, Ruhiger als im Heli und natürlich der unschlagbare Preis.

Unsere Entscheidung viel auf Air Ventures wegen der ausgezeichneten Bewertungen auf TripAdvisor. Das auch zurecht:

- Pilotin war Top, gab Tipps für Ausflüge und erklärte während des Flugs alles. Außerdem war sie sehr aufmerksam dass beide Seiten des Flugzeuges alles zu sehen und zu Fotografieren bekamen.

-Das Flugzeug ist klein und Familiär, man hält Kontakt zueinander und mit dem Piloten via Headset. Wir waren nur 5 Passagiere an Board von maximal 6, von den Plätzen sieht man überall perfekt!

-Kontakt lief reibungslos über E-Mail, die Dame vom Büro war auch sehr nett und zuvorkommend. Man bekommt sogar Getränke und kalte Tücher (falls einem übel wird)

Wir würden allen die nach Kaua‘i kommen empfehlen diesen Flug zu machen, zumal man einen Überblick über die Insel bekommt und tolle Tipps von der Crew!

🤙🏻🤙🏻

Review Text: We  saw stunning views of Waimea Canyon and the NaPali coast, as well as the rest of the beautiful island of Kauai, 74% of which can only be viewed by air, according to our friendly pilot. Air Ventures was able to accommodate our date on very short notice - super service!  After a brief safety review, we were placed into our seats to evenly distribute weight throughout the plan, which seats six plus the pilot.  The flight was very pleasant and the pilot was quite informative.  I had found some of our helicopter tours on other islands to cause slight motion sickness due to the vibration. I had no problem with this flight - the plan ride was smooth and serene.  The only downside is that they did not record the flight for purchase later, which both of our helicopter tours had done.  Still, what a great way to view this gorgeous island paradise and create lifetime memories!  A must do!

Review Text: My friend and I were in Kauai celebrating our 50th birthdays and wanted to do something memorable together. When our commercial plane arrived in Lihue, we saw this yellow bi-plane parked near where we taxied in to our gate. We both said we needed to look into that!!!! So we did and booked a flight with our very experienced pilot Kevin. We were so excited to be doing this flight, but Kevin made it even more exciting for us. He taught us everything we needed to know pre-flight and then even after take off he was able to communicate with us through the headsets we had. He gave a wonderful description of everything we flew over...this included the resort area, up to Waimea Canyon (where we flew right down the middle!), came back over the coastline to the Napoli Coast. To add some excitement to our flight, and because we asked him to, he did a flight maneuver with us! Actually did a loopity loop over the water! All we good was giggle with excitement!!!! The tour continued over Princeville/Hanalei and then turned into the center of the island where we flew around the volcano, saw numerous waterfalls, including Wailua Falls! I cannot say enough about how fun and interesting this flight was to see so much of the island and to get such a detailed commentary from Kevin! I highly recommend this flight!

Review Title: Great flight today in the Waco Bi-plane.  Beautiful scenery and an adventure in the plane!
Review Text: So first, I'm a private pilot (just two years since licensed).  When sitting on the beach a few days ago, I heard this unusual engine sound and looked up and saw a bright yellow bi-plane flying over and thought "I have to do that!".  A little research led me to Air Ventures and their brand-new (2017) bi-plane.  It's a beautiful airplane - basically a very modern version of a classic bi-plane design.  I had absolutely no concern about the safety of the aircraft - in fact it's maneuverability made it the perfect platform for sightseeing.  Our pilot was great - obviously very experienced and safe but also a great tour guide.  If you're an aviation buff, I would highly recommend this - really a unique experience blended with seeing the natural beauty of Kauai.  There are a few things to be aware of though - it is an open cockpit aircraft that seats two reasonably sized people in the front.  It's noisy, though it's mostly obviated by the headset/cloth helmet you get to wear (and look swanky).  Photos with your phone can be done if you rent a plastic enclosure ($5) from them for safety reasons.  My daughter's phone had a few problems focusing through the case.  So there are certainly more comfortable options for a flight tour (also at Air Ventures), but I can't think of another that is quite the adventure.  Highly recommended if you're into this sort of thing.

Review Text: Kevin the pilot and his staff were super friendly. The preflight briefing was quick and you get a good walk around of the plane. Once we were up the views were spectacular, the ride was smooth and the commentary from Kevin was incredibly historic and factual while maintaining a great level of humor. We saw parts of the isle not accessible by car or boat and famous movie back drops (including Scaramanga's secret beach in gold finger). The open cockpit gave a sense of classic adventure that you could only get in a biplane. The cool temperatures made the ride very comfortable and the views of volcanoes and waterfalls seemed endless. I highly recommend this tour over a helicopter tour, mainly because of the ambiance and the fact that you sit in front of the pilot so your view is unobscured. Take offs and landings were perfect and short, Kevin is a true and experienced pilot. All in all a great experience! 10/10 would charter "Woodstock" again!

Review Title: Great price, but very different experience from than a helicopter.
Review Text: The captain and staff at AirVentures was very friendly. My husband and I did the air and luau combo, which was a great deal for what you are suppose to get. I did a lot of research on helicopter flights and planes like the one at AirVentures, and ideally they all show you the same sights around the island, but you will pay an arm and a leg for a helicopter ride. Unfortunately, the day we went was pretty cloudy and rainy, which I had asked if it would affect our route for the trip and I was told "we wouldn't take you on the flight if it wasn't going to be worth your time and money." One of the main sights I was looking forward to seeing was the "Jurassic Falls" and some of the other Falls that are unable to be seen by foot or car. The weather did end up keeping us from seeing some of these sights, which I personally felt made it not worth the money. My husband and I opted to pay the extra $25 to attach our GoPro to the wing of the plane, which captured some great footage, however I think I was able to see more from the GoPro video, than from the actual flight. My husband sat in the front next to the captain, and I sat directly behind the captain. There is no air(just a small fan) in the cabin, and it was very stuffy and uncomfortable. Unfortunately because I was seated behind the captain, I felt as though I was unable to get a great view of the sights, since everything was mostly on the passenger side of the plane. Overall it wasn't a horrible experience, but its definitely not the same experience as a helicopter. I noticed during the flight and during a hike on the NaPali coast later that week, that the helicopters take their passengers much closer into each beautiful valley along the coast, and you get a much more up close experience of some of the falls and beautiful sights that Kauai has to offer. Make sure you do your research and know exactly what you're wanting to see and what kind of experience you want. AirVentures was great, the flight was very smooth, especially the landing, but you certainly get what you pay for since you're only paying 1/3 of the cost of a helicopter ride!

Review Text:
This review is for the 1130AM biplane ride with Kevin - the mustachioed pilot. We began by getting an up-close view and detailed overview of the brand new biplane that Air Ventures purchased in 2017. That thing is a beauty! Kevin made sure we safely boarded the two side-by-side seats in the front of the biplane and got us set up with our old-school caps with headphones, mic, and optional goggles. The headset is very comfortable and easy to use - although you need to be careful to speak loudly and to keep your mic out of the wind so you can hear Kevin's narration.

Within 5 minutes of taking off, we already had amazing mountain views and it only got better from there. It was great to be able to take in all the spectacular sights without having to look through a window and to breath in the fresh air and touch the clouds! We were concerned that such a small plane might have a bumpy ride, but it was smooth sailing except for maybe 1 or 2 brief moments when we were turning over Waimea canyon.

If you're staying on the North Shore, being able to see the breathtaking views of the Waimea canyon without having to make the 3-4 hour trip would be enough to justify the cost of admission by itself. The awesome overview of the Na Pali coast and all the highlights around the island just makes the deal even sweeter.

One recommendation - if you're going to bring a DSLR camera like we did, you may have better luck with a telescopic lens, since my wife had some difficulty snapping good pictures with her regular lens because she was trying to reach over my shoulder to snap the pictures. If you have a GoPro camera, you can bring it and mount it on the plane for $25 or so - I would highly recommend that.

Overall, this is a must do attraction that I wish I had done earlier! 5 stars!

Review Title: Biplane tour is the way to go.
Review Text: We drove up to see the Napali valleys from the lookout and it was completely cloudy.  Very disappointing.  However, I had already booked a biplane tour before our trip.  I'm so glad I did.  First - I got to cross "fly in a biplane" off my bucket list.  That alone was awesome.  Second - we got to see the entire island in the course of an hour, including the Napali coast.  I've ridden in helicopters and closed prop planes.  The down side is that if you're not on the side facing the attraction it will be difficult for you to see.  In the biplane it's just two of you and you can both see out in all directions.  Kevin narrated the entire trip so we knew what we were looking at and he made sure we got to see everything.  We even stuck our hands out in a cloud so we could say we touched a cloud (nice suggestion, Kevin).  The highlight had to be flying in the crater of Mt. Kawaikini and seeing all of the waterfalls. Las mejores vistas son desde la derecha, aunque se aprecia bien desde la izquierda, pero si se puede elegir... Antes del vuelo preguntan quien quiere ir delante con el piloto. Se empieza por la costa hacia Poipu, se va hacia el interior viendo el cañón del Waimea, se recorre la costa de Napali y la costa norte, para volver al interior y al aeropuerto. Una hora en total. Review Title: A Must To See the 90% of the Island You Can;t From The Road
Review Text: You can only see 10% of Kauai from the road in a vehicle.  By airplane is the best way to see the rest of the Island.  Captain Roy was great.  We flew a few hundred feet above ridges of the mountains, so close that you could easily see people walking on the trails.  No, they weren't ant size!  The plane was small air conditioned, and everyone had a window seat.  There were also cold towels for people who got overheated by the greenhouse effect of their large window.  Captain Roy talked to everyone as we flew along and we talked back as we saw things for everyone else to look at.  I would suggest that you use the washroom before the flight, as the flight is an hour long especially if you've had a few cups of Kona or Kauai coffer or pints of Kona or Kauai beer.  Photo ops galore:  taking off and landing and of course everywhere on the island below you!

Review Title: Copter versus Fixed Wing Tours - I've Done Both
Review Text:
I've done at least a dozen copter tours on the islands and now this is my 2nd fixed wing tour. I know another reviewer disagrees on some points, but here's my take based on my fixed wing experience today:
Fixed wing over copter:
1. Price... I paid less than half for a tour that covered much of the same areas as the similar length copter tours. HALF! -
2. Comfort - Much roomier than most copters.
3. Window - Everyone has a window seat. Not always true on even the 4 seat copters as 2 of you on the small copter may be in the front seat (meaning one of your windows is the front of the windshield.But, sometimes parts of the plane may invade your photos. Least view impairment is with a fixed wing plane with the wing on top.
4. Feeling of being solid - I LOVE copter tours especially as the doors off tours, but there are moments of jerks and vibration that you don't have on the fixed wing plane.

Copter beats fixed wing tour:
1. Copters in Hawaii tend to go up more canyons which allow more ops to see water falls.
2. At certain places, the copter may choose to hover and turn to allow you an optimal view or photo op (Jack Harter Tours on Kauai has a tour 30 minutes longer than most that does this a lot)
3. When all is said and done, I think the view from the 3 outside window seats is slightly better especially when you fly a doors-off copter tour.

Summary: I think the fixed wing tour is an excellent way to get the wonders of the islands from the air, yet save enough per couple for 2 or 3 high-end dinners here. If you're a bit timid about air tours, I think the fixed wing is less intimidating. I think the best photo op experiences remains the copters with doors off, but certainly one can get credible photos from the fixed wing.

Review Text:
We took a flight last week on the Big Island and had so totally enjoyed it that we decided to do it again on the Island of Kauai. We were a bit concerned about the weather (It rained earlier and it was windy) but our pilot, Eric, said that all would be well (This is a guy with an interesting sense of humor!). Thankfully, it was all okay.
Eric assigned me to the co-pilot's seat (right side, next to the pilot) with the wife immediately behind me. He placed the two other passengers behind my wife so all of the passengers were on the right side of the plane (The plane, the plane!). And yes, he flew us past the Fantasy Island Falls, plus the film sites of Elvis's Blue Hawaii, and Harrison Ford's 6 Day, 7 Nights movie. Oh yeah, he flew us around the entire island and also headed inland to see the Grand Canyon of the Pacific. (And the good Lord parted the clouds so we could see it lit up and how perfectly He painted the area!)
Overall, the flight was smooth. Yes, there were a few bumps along the way (Eric calls them 'texture'), and after one bump, he kiddingly asked me what I touched in the co-pilot's chair. (Of course he had an ear-to-ear smile when he made the crack.)
This is a trip you can take by either airplane, biplane or helicopter, and it is a trip you won't want to miss!
Enjoy...
Aloha!

Review Text:
I had wanted to fly in a biplane most all of my life, I'm 60 years old, but I just had never done so. While researching for a trip to Kauai for my wife and me I came across Air Ventures' “YMF-5 Super” Waco biplane and knew that was the ride for me. My wife was a bit apprehensive about riding in a small, open-cockpit airplane. I assured her that she would love it, and boy did she!
Our pilot, Harry, briefed about the airplane itself, and about the flight that we were about to leave on. After a few photos we were strapped in; the headphones plugged in and working, and we were off.
The day was a cloudy one, with the clouds clinging to the ridges and mountaintops all the way around the island. It mattered not one bit. The views were still incredible. I knew the plane would not be the best photography platform, but we still got numerous good photos. I would not recommend taking a tele- of any kind. Shoot wide-angle with a long focus. For us, though, this was not a photo trip, photos were an added bonus, but a ride of a lifetime.
The ride in an open-cockpit biplane just can't be beat, and to do it over and around Kauai was even better than my expectations. The roar of the American-made rotary seven-cylinder engine, and the wind ruffling about provided a very tactile experience, such as I have never experienced in small planes or helicopters.
All along, Harry kept us informed as to what we were seeing, and he was able to give us pieces of the histories of the Hawaiian peoples associated with them.
If you want close up to the waterfalls and cliff faces, or are looking to take the ultimate photograph, then maybe a ride in Air Ventures' “YMF-5 Super” Waco may not be for you. But, if you want to have the biggest grin that will fit on your face when you climb back out of the plane, then this trip fits the bill.
Thanks to all the employees of Ventures for their attention and kindness, and a special "Mahalo" to Harry for the ride. Aloha!!

Review Text: An airborne tour of Kauai is an essential part of your trip to this island.  You cannot appreciate its beauty from the ground no matter how good the weather is.  Yes, helicopters are more maneuverable but they are more expensive and one had unfortunately crashed into Pearl Harbor during our visit to Oahu which closed the water shuttle to the Arizona memorial during our stay.  AirVentures Cessna fixed wing airplanes are an excellent compromise.  They are surprisingly maneuverable and our pilot, Eric, with over 7000 flying hours, was as safe a "driver" as he was an entertaining narrator.  We saw whales at 1000'; we saw Waimea canyon as you will never see it from the road and Eric's tour of the Na Pali coast was incredible.  The grand finale was a flyby the Wailua falls (Da Plen!, Da Plen!).  Book morning flights- clouds cause more problems in the PM.  Do this trip first for an overview or last to fill in the details but do it! Oh, BTW, sit on the right side of the plane for best views. Aloha!

Review Text:
Gwen and I are first time Kauai visitors and we are glad we decided to take an AirVentures Hawaii Kauai air tour. The cost seemed very reasonable and the description of the tour found on the AirVentures website was very descriptive. Our amicable pilot Ray greeted all 5 of us passengers in the office and we shared a discussion about our flight itinerary. Our pilot is a very experienced aviator who has spent considerable time exploring the island and loves each flight he takes. He was excited explaining how fortunate we were to be taking this particular tour because areas he wanted to share with us he had only seen a few times in his many years of flying as the weather was clear allowing for exceptional viewing. He was right! Wow! Not only was the sightseeing good but he was very knowledgeable of the land areas below us,..landmarks we saw,.. beautiful valleys both arid and lush hues of green..,the waterfalls and river watersheds,..land use and development ... favorite beaches...movie sets...the coastline...plants and gardens...celebrities...and even a whale!!! We were family aboard this eco-friendly airvan and could communicate with each other and plenty of viewing and picture taking all around. The adventure lasted longer than we had anticipated and the worst part was having to return to our earthbound habitat. But wait that was not the end of our tour as our pilot reminisced about the company and his planes and his relationship as a friend and mechanic with the late Aloha vet who is one of my wife's favorite animal friendly tv celebrities! What a small world sometimes. We slowly ambled back into the office and even the friendly staff gave us tips on where to eat lunch!
Mahalo nui loa...Ahui hou!
Gwen and Dana

Every flight is going to be different, we knew that from watching the view change while we were standing for 10 minutes at an overlook in Kokee park, but there was only one canyon he didn't take us into because it was still very cloudy and raining in there, but instead we saw and shot photos of a crazy amazing rainbow. While over the north coast area we saw a whale breach, and for awhile it stayed just under the surface, where we could see the whole length of it for awhile, omg, you have no idea how big those guys are until you're on top of one.it was like a glass aquarium show from above or something! Eric kept checking in on how my hubby was in the back, warned us when we'd be getting "texture" from the rain, but really was not as turbulent as is expected, just two or three times of bumps and the take off and landing were gentle.I even got to take the controls for awhile! If you're on Kauai you have to fly with Air Ventures!

Review Text:
Today, I took my 11-year-old grandkid for a ride with pilot Kevin on a one-hour flight over all of Kauai. I loved it, and she enjoyed it even more.
The airplane, which would be easier to enter if you're a contortionist, is actually quite comfortable once seated, Kevin is a terrific pilot who makes sure his passengers get to see all that Kauai offers from about 1,500 feet, and he keeps up a running commentary that's quite interesting.
He detoured a bit so we could see some whales off the north end of the Napali coast, and watching them breach was a thrill. The view from up there is exquisite - they don't call Kauai the garden island for nothing.
The flight was smooth and comfortable. I'd worried about being cold, given air rushing by at 100 mph and us being in an open aircraft, but no worries -- you can wear shorts and flip-flops if you want and you'll be fine.
Conventional cameras with straps are fine, too, but put away your cell phone once you taxi for takeoff -- too easy for them to tumble from the airplane.
The ground crew is great -- taking time before and especially after the flight to use your cameras to take your photos with the biplane.
All in all, a great experience. Was it worth $440 for the two of us? If you could see the expression on the young girl's face you'd know the answer to that one.
Highly recommended.

Review Title: Red Barron through the skies of Kauai
Review Text:
We recently spent 10 days in Kauai. The Red Barron biplane tour was an amazing addition to our trip. Harry, our pilot was so patient. First he made time for plenty of photo shoots with us and the plane. Harry even posed for a picture. Then he carefully mounted our GoPro to the wing strut. He made suggestions for settings for the best pictures. Then after climbing in the front seats of the plane we were amazed with the most gorgeous views of Kauai from the air. Harry was narrating often, letting us know about the views below. He would circle areas so we could get a better view or take in all the details. We were wearing canvas helmets with radio communication with each other and Harry. This made it easy to ask Harry questions, make comments or ask for clarification.

We debated between the biplane and helicopter tours. Both are about the same length of time. The helicopters do get closer to the falls but I read so many bad reviews about seating and glass glare. Neither of these can be an issue in an open cockpit and with only 2 seats besides the pilot seat. Our thoughts were that we could take a helicopter tour anywhere but where else would we ever get this option of a very cool biplane.

The staff and owners of Air Ventures are pretty amazing too. When I asked for advise on lunch they recommended a great fish & chips restaurant. Nothing was rushed here. Everyone took the time to make sure we had a great time there but also on the rest of our trip - Thank you.

I would highly recommend this tour to anyone visiting Kauai. Schedule it early in your trip so you can get ideas of where to drive to later in your trip.

Review Text:
Our family of 5 took a flight today around Kauai - it was a more economical option than a helicopter tour. PROs: we got the plane to ourselves, it only seats 6 passengers, the weather was clear and mostly sunny, we got beautiful views of the island and our pilot Harry did turns on the major sites like Waimea Canyon and Na Pali coast to allow both sides of plane to get good views, and the tour felt very personalized with just our family in there.
CONs: you don't get as close to sights as a helicopter.

As far as seating goes, the best seat for pictures is the co-pilot chair up in front, similar to helicopters. Anything behind may have some obstruction by the wing but you can still get nice views. The ride was relatively smooth - we went at 8:30am - but afterwards we all felt a little motion sickness from the ride and went back to hotel to rest. Recommend you check the weather forecast and choose the sunniest day of your trip, and start in the morning. We noticed it often rained in afternoon.

Final verdict: I recommend this for getting aerial tour of island, especially if helicopter is too pricey. It was enjoyable with great views.

Review Text: This is clearly the highlight of any of my 3 trips to Hawaii while visiting 4 of the Islands. Whichever helicopter tour you choose probably doesn't matter, there are hundreds it seems and they are interesting. I've done 7 so far, 3 in Hawaii and others in other parts of the world. This Bi-plane is just another thing altogether. Open cockpit and throaty engine really gives a different experience. Also, consider that in a helicopter the chances are that you will end up in one of the back middle seat in a vibrating bubble. On this flight you get right or left and full front view. Our pilot Paul put us through some thrilling maneuvers at different points during the tour and I could just go back and do this again and again. I have a gopro and used their mount. It was perfect, however I did pull out my phone to record some of those fun turns and drops and climbs. I would recommend that if you can, try to record from your seat, but come prepared to secure your camera to your body. I didn't secure my phone but gripped it until my knuckles were white and certainly kept it behind the windscreen since it was clear that if I stuck it into the wind, it would rip it from my hand.
