Review Title: FANTASTIC Full-Island Kauai Air Tour w/ GREAT Informative Pilot
Review Text:
I had the pleasure of a late afternoon "The Big Kahuna" air tour this week with Air Ventures Hawaii that was a FANTASTIC full tour of Kauai.

The views from the plane were amazing and the pilot Brian was outstanding. With headsets on he provided me and the 3 others on the plance an amazing historical, geographic, geological and current events explanation that highlighted everything we saw and importantly he did so with great delivery and with good doses of humor too.

On Kauai everyone has multiple options to tour from above by airplane or helicopter and since I grew up in a family where my father flew small private planes as a hobby his whole life and it's how we traveled on vacations on the mainland, I really wanted to experience Kauai from above in a plane and I can tell you that this fixed-wing air tour did NOT disappoint. In fact, I was blown away by how much I saw in Air Venture's roomy GA-8 Airvan with large windows, comfortable seating and air-conditioning I believe. It was comfortable!

After take-off the plane headed South and this is only some of the things we saw -- the incredible Kipu Kai shoreline, Poipu, Olokele Canyon (I actually saw the famed Robinson family's house!), many different angles & views of the Waimea Canyon which is a MUST for any Kauai visitor and then an outstanding tour or the
Nā Pali coast. Brian, our pilot was flawless with his detail and was really entertaining about all these sites and more. The view of the "cathedrals" along the Nā Pali coast was very amazing!

We then wrapped around the North Shore at Ke'e Beach which is the end of the road on North Shore & start of the 12-mille ea. way Kalalau Trail along the Nā Pali coast. Extending the North Shore we then had amazing views of Tunnels Beach, Ha'ena, Lumaha'i Beach, Hanalei & all Hanalei Bay...and then Princeville.

Brian then flew us inland up the Hanalei River valley & as close as we could get to Mount Waiʻaleʻale at over 5,000 feet, almost always shrouded in clouds as it was for us, on the summit as this is one of the wettest spots in the world with over 600 inches of rain per year.

Just think GREEN & BLUE because this is what you will see.

GREEN because that is what you see on this airplane tour of the many remote places on the land of Kauai and BLUE for all the beautiful water you see and then including beaches, reefs, Hanalei valley & taro fields, the Wailua River and TONS of waterfalls.

After the interior tours both on the West side and the North Shore, we then came into the back side of Kapaa over mountains with even more waterfall views & then beautiful views of East side beaches before landing in Lihue.

Air Ventures and pilot Brian are to be commended for running an outstanding tour, at least the one that I experienced. I would recommend this to anyone of any age from anywhere. It was just a fantastic experience.

Mahalo Air Ventures Hawaii... :)

Review Text:
Took a 70 minute flight with my two young daughters, the Gippsland GA8 (airvan) is a comfortable aircraft, each passenger has a bubble window suitable for photography, and cold bottled water is available throughout the flight. Guests were provided with headsets and could interact with the pilot at any time over the intercom.
As the flight departed Lihue, our pilot Paul was quick to point out features such as Mount Waialeale, Wailua falls (Fantasy Island), the Kilohana Crater, Poipu Beach, along with the Kauai Coffee plantation. As we travelled along the black sands of Waimea (with the forbidden island of Nihau visible), we turned north for a spectacular tour of the Waimea Canyon and the many waterfalls along the way. One of the more thrilling moments of the tour is occurs when the jagged cathedral hilltops fall away to reveal the Napali coast, on this flight we were lucky enough to spot a couple of grey whales breaching. Our flight circled the Taro fields and waters of Hanalei Bay, where our pilot pointed out some of the homes of the wealthy and famous. We continued east toward Kilauea lighthouse and wildlife sanctuary prior to continuing south passing features such as the Sleeping Giant, Fern Grotto, and the Wailua River.
Our pilot's narrative was highly informative in terms of local island history, natural history, popular culture, geology, and current events. He also offered up some of his own opinions on great spots for surfing, snorkeling, and meal choices. I would highly recommend this flight as one of your first activities on Kauai as it provides not only a visual feast, but a brief yet thorough education on what sets the Garden Isle apart from the others.

Review Text:
My husband and I did the bi-plane tour with Pilot Paul. This is a great tour for people who have been to Kauai many times and would like something different to do as well as for those who are adventurous. It is not, however, for the faint of heart. I love small planes but the open cockpit was rather uncomfortable for me. My husband loved it and would do it again; for me, it was a once-in-a-lifetime experience. It was quite windy the day we went and since the bi-plane is so light, we were bounced around pretty good. The pilot did a couple of hammerhead stalls which were like being on a roller coaster. If you love roller coasters, you'll love this. Unfortunately, I hate them! The highlight of the trip was seeing two whales breach below us. Paul circled several times when he spotted them and we couldn't believe it when two of them came out of the water at the same time. This is not a good trip for taking photos. I wish I had given the camera to my husband because he's much taller and sat up over the side of the plane and could have taken pictures. I was too terrified to sit up and lean over to do that and I couldn't get the camera strap from around my neck (because of the headphones) once we were in the air.

My husband id 6'5" and had plenty of leg room. It is the width of the plane that could cause problems. Neither of us are overweight but because my husband is a big guy, we were quite snug in the seat. Getting in and out of the plane is a challenge, even more so for the second person in who will also be the first person out. Two large people definitely would not fit in the seat.

Paul's commentary during the tour was very informative. This was our fourth trip to Kauai; we always enjoy learning new facts about the island as well as refreshing our memory about things we learned on previous trips.

If you like adventures, by all means take this tour. Just be aware that it is not for everyone.

Review Title: No experience with the tour due to Mother Nature, but the customer service is EXCELLENT!
Review Text:
I was referred to this company by another that I had tried to book but they were full. I looked on their website first and found a GREAT deal, and called for more information. I spoke with Pua, and she really is a shining star for that company! She was really helpful, kind, overflowing with aloha, and wonderful to talk to in general. She answered all of my questions (I was concerned about weight limits because my other half and I are bigger folks) and somehow got us even more excited about the trip. When we booked, she asked how much we each weighed and assured us it was only for the pilot’s information to maintain safety and balance on the aircraft. It was not an issue in the least, which was another reason we went with them. Though there was some confusion about a transportation issue, because I saw it on the website she graciously and immediately honored it. Turns out they’d recently changed the special on the website and she hadn’t heard about it yet, but she even called me back after booking to thank me for bringing it to her attention.

The day before our trip, she called me to confirm. I always appreciate when a company calls me to confirm things. She noted how I sounded less stressed than the last time she’d spoken to me. She was right – when I’d spoken to her to book I was very stressed trying to organize a (long-awaited) vacation and finish things up at home, and when I spoke to her I’d just finished getting a massage after a week aboard a cruise ship.

The day of the tour, we did have a delay in getting picked up from the meeting spot (an unknown delay with the shuttle driver) but we called Pua and she was on it. It was raining, which we expected since it’s Kauai, but when we did get a ride to the airport, Pua informed us (with an obviously heavy heart) that because of the storm, the flight had just been cancelled prior to our arrival at the airport. The weather conditions made flying not only dangerous but impractical since we wouldn’t be able to see anything anyway. She felt really bad about it and offered alternative activities and offered to find us a rental car, give us a ride to the Fern Grotto, or back to the pickup point, she found a map of the island and showed us where we could find really beautiful, interesting things. On an island where the mountains are the main attraction, we were impressed with her recommendations for finding ground-level attractions.
She left us to discuss and decide what we wanted to do, and was incredibly sympathetic to our plight. We were on a cruise and only had a few hours on the island. We hadn’t researched anything else because we’d found the tour early on in our planning and gone with it. Should we have had a contingency plan? Probably. But hindsight is 20/20. We decided to make the best of the situation anyway. Pua took pictures of us with the headsets on against the backdrop of the rainy mountain (what you could see of it, which wasn’t much), and all in all made our visit with her well worth our time.

In the end we decided against renting a car or going to the Fern Grotto on our own, and went back to the pickup point, which was a set of shops. We went behind the shops and found a great little bay that we practically had to ourselves. It was very nice.
If we ever find ourselves going to Kauai again, without hesitation we will DEFINITELY book this trip again, if for no other reason than Pua’s customer service was so excellent that it made “return” customers of us!

Review Title: Bring a heavy camera for the biplane!
Review Text:
I knew there was a lot to see in Kauai and much of it is not accessible by car so I wanted to book a trip to view it all from the air. I stumbled upon the biplane tour and was sold. How cool to get to fly in a biplane! Even better we got to see so much of Kauai from the air and it was just the two of us! Since the plane is so small it just fits 2 passengers and the pilot so no jostling people you don't know for a better view and no chance of getting stuck in the middle or back! The price was reasonable too.

It rained quite a bit yesterday and my weather app predicted more rain today so I was a bit worried we wouldn't have a good ride but I was wrong! The weather cleared up just before take off and because of all the rain yesterday we were able to see waterfalls that are dry most of the year! The tour started with a view of the southern coast and worked out way around the island counter clockwise. Our pilot was super laid back and wanted to make sure we had a good show. Minutes after take off he spotted some whales off the coast and deviated from his original path to circle around so we could get a better view! I was worried we'd miss the whales while we were here but I saw them! We flew over all of the major sites, the lush green valleys, the canyons, the Na Pali coast and everything in between! We saw the Jurassic water fall (along with about 50 other waterfalls throughout the flight) and plenty of rainbows. The cool thing about rainbows from the air is that they form full circles!

They offer the option to attach your gopro camera to the plane wing, do it, even though it costs a little extra! I was on the fence about it but ended up paying for the service and I'm glad I did. I would have pooped my pants worrying about filming from the plane, the wind is super powerful and I felt like it was going to rip my little point and shoot from my hands the whole time! If you bring a camera tape it to your hands or bring something with weight! The view from the gopro on the wing is much better too. There are lots of wing parts in the way of you try to take photos from the plane. My husband had a big camera, I haven't seen his photos yet but I know my photos have lots of wing struts in them.

Overall this is probably the best thing we've done in Hawaii. If you're going to take a plane ride over Kauai take the biplane tour!

Review Title: Left that Omen in the Clouds
Review Text:
My husband and I said we would NEVER fly in a small plane due to safety issues. Well, there were two ways to see Kauai from the air, helicopter or a small plane which was operated with Air Ventures. We decided on the plane. We set out from Princeville three hours ahead of time, wanted to do some additional sightseeing on the south end of the island. We arrived at Air Venture around 2:20 for our 3pm flight. When we arrived the young lady apologized because our flight was delayed an hour due to staffing issues. The delay did not pose a problem for us, we had some other things that we could do to fill the time. The only problem it did cause, it made me think is this an omen? We returned 10 minute before our schedule time and my husband attempted to check in. This is where the real problem came into play, the young lady that had greeted us before was having a personal conversation with another worker from another vendor and continued her conversation for about 5-7 minutes while my husband stood there. Then she turns around and says how over worked she had been that day and she had just cleared her desk. My husband is not one to hold his tongue and told her she couldn’t have just cleared her desk because he had been standing there waiting while she was having a personal conversation that she had started before he walked in. Of course by then he was ready to cancel the tour due to the delay and his wait to check in. After we talked we decide to take the tour.
I did inform the pilot, I believe his name was John, of my fear of flying in a small plane. He did insure me that I would enjoy my tour and he would take care of me.
First, the take off was smooth, beautifully executed. I did not know we had left the ground, until I looked down. The narrative was very good, he pointed out many interesting towns and sites with explanation. When he went over an area where he knew we would get turbulent winds he would let us know, so that we would be prepared. I appreciated the preparation and it calmed my fears. The landed was as smooth as the take off. You could tell that John loved his job and took pride in what he did. It was a great tour. And that omen, I left it up in the clouds. For our inconvenience (flight delay) we were given a DVD of what we saw on the tour, it was a prerecorded DVD. I am rating this tour a 4 and not a 5 because of the office person. But, the tour and John our pilot were more than a 5.

Review Title: Great Value for a Safe and Smooth Ride
Review Text: Like other reviewers, I did my share of research.  We debated over the helicopter options as well.  Frankly, the majority of the helicopter options are twice the price of Air Ventures.  Air Ventures is a great value.  If you want the experience of being in a helicopter, then it may be worth it to pay the premium, but note that in a helicopter, it's not a consistent, smooth ride - you're constantly going up and down.  I did notice that helicopters seemed to be able to fly a bit lower and closer to the sites but not by much.  What I liked most about Air Ventures is that it's a very stable ride; there's not a lot of ascending and descending.  Overall, I definitely recommend Air Ventures - best value, and a safe, one hour ride around Kauai.  You can pretty much see the whole island in one hour.    This is also a great tour for the kids.  The Pilot sat the kids down in the captain's chairs and we were able to take pictures of them.  Highly recommended and do the tour in the beginning of your stay in Kauai as others have recommended.

Review Title: Good value and experience but could improve
Review Text: I was bringing my family of six with kids age 9 to 17 to Kauai on a special trip and did a lot of research on potential flights to see the Napali coast and more. AirAdventures offers a great value as the price is significantly lower than the helicopter options... and as others have noted...everyone gets a window seat. When we arrived, the reception was a bit too laid back in my opinion. We were on time...not early...yet no one was there to engage us and when someone did come out....even with just us there...they didn't welcome us or engage us. My family thought we were in the wrong place. Eventually they checked us in. The flight itself was good....smoother than expected. One of the six felt stomach nausea which is to be expected. But the pilots only comment before boarding was to be sure to use the bags so no one would throw up on him as a girl had recently done. (Not the warmest comment) More notably, there are two aspects that others have noted that others should be prepared for. First off, all the sights are seen from the right side....so the members of my family on the left side were notably disappointed. There didn't seem to be any acknowledgement about that nor any attempt to swing around to allow the left side to see top sites well. The other limitation as noted by others, is how garbled the sound is from the headphone system used. One really has to strain their listening to hear the pilot through the heavy static and that leaves a lot to potentially miss in the experience. I know that all helicopters and planes have limited sound in the headphone system but this seemed harder to hear than usual. All in all... a worthwhile experience...not at all the highlight of our trip as others speak of their flights....in part because the crew didn't seem to treat it like a big choice to go flying. But the beauty is stunning, the extent of the island seen is good, and the price much more affordable than the helicopters.

Review Text: This is a great way to see Kauai that is more economical than the helicopter tours, about half the price. We are a little older and felt that the helicopter a bit much, plus it boiled down to our what our travel budget can handle.  In our opinion, the argument that if you'd made it to Hawaii, then you should be able to afford a helicopter ride is really false, we all have price points.  Air Ventures provides you basically the same flight itinerary and for a lot less money.  For those environmentally conscience, the fuel used by Air Ventures is a fraction of what a helicopter uses. Review Text: The overall experience was good. There is a fuel surcharge of about $16 dollars that you must pay once you arrive so have some cash  or credit card ready. You are provided with a microphone so you can communicate with the pilot and an aviation headset so that you can hear the pilot. The only recommendation I have for the Air Ventures Hawaii team is to update the in-flight communications system so that passengers don't have to hear air-traffic communications during their flight and also hear less static coming through the headphones. It was a little hard to understand the pilot sometimes. Other than that, I recommend this to anyone wishing to get an up-and-close look at most of the island and its beautiful landmarks. When considering either a helicopter or plane ride, remember that while helicopters can get you much closer to landmarks, Air Ventures Hawaii planes fly very low too (~1,000 ft) and can cover much more of the island. My husband sat copilot seat and I sat behind the pilot. There is AC and everyone wears headphones that the pilots talks to you through and you can ask questions through. The pilot was extremely knowledgeable and we learned so much about so many things on the island. He was funny too, it was the best.

We took our phones and our professional camera with us and it was steady enough to get smooth video and clear pictures, we took tons and it was so amazing. He flies back and forth to make sure both sides of the plane get the same view on most parts of the island, which I really appreciated.

I recommend you do this at the start of your trip! We did this on the last day and we realized how many cool places we never explored after taking the air tour, had we only known before. Either way, take this tour, you will not be sorry and everyone you know at home will be so jealous!

Review Title: Fly Kauai: Experience of a lifetime
Review Text: We did this the last day of our honeymoon, and it was spectacular! The views are stunning, and it is really nice to be able to get some perspective on the size of the island, and where things are. I would recommend doing this at least a few days into your trip, or after you have had the chance to explore the outskirts of the island, so that you can orient yourself better. Our tour was $125/person, a great deal in comparison to the helicopter rides, which were upwards of $235/person. The ONLY downside is that on our particular flight, we had a person who got sick and we found out what she had for lunch. :( So - due to possible turbulence, you may want to take some motion sickness medication before you go on this tour. But - the Na Pali coast, Waimea Canyon, Hanapepe Canyon, "Jurassic" Falls and Kalalau Valley are stunning from the air, and you get to see places where 'Pirates of the Caribbean' and other movies were filmed. You get to see places that are only accessible by hiking; so if you are short on time, this is an excellent option. One thing I would mention is that there is NOTHING like seeing Kauai from the air. Nothing. We did a sunset dinner cruise to the Na Pali coast, and - though beautiful - it was a totally different experience from the air.

Review Text:
Awesome experience! This was the highlight of our trip to Kauai. My son and I took the 45 minute biplane tour. It was a nice calm clear day, perfect for flying. Our pilot Nick was outstanding! While he was narrating each area we flew over, he added some insight to its significance. For example, he showed us where the original pineapple plantations were located and explained why they have since relocate them to Maui.

I've been on two helicopter tours on Kauai before and this was a better, more personal experience for me (only 2 passengers at a time) with the open cockpit. Yes, the helicopters may get you closer to some of the landmarks and perhaps better photo opps,,,, but at a much higher price, and I've found those pilots' narration to be quite dull.

Nick gave us a lot of information about the island and the two way communication setup allowed us to ask questions. One of the best parts was when he pulled some high G turns
and some "wing overs" for us. The ride was very exhilarating! I would definitely recommend this as a must do for visitors.

Review Title: Incredible Way to See the Island
Review Text:
I have taken two flights with Air Ventures while in Kauai and this is about the only way that you will see the island in its entirety - in the air. Much of the island is inaccessible and to get a real idea of this incredible paradise, plan to see it by air.

The plane trip is the perfect length as you fly to all parts of the island. You'll see the Napali Costline and the Canyon up close on this venture. In fact, we were able to see hundreds of whales in the ocean below during our last flight. I'm a bit of a fraidy cat when it comes to heights and small planes, but the scenery helps one to overcome that obstacle quickly. One caveat - if there are a lot of clouds and any rain, you WILL experience some bumps on the flight.

The pilot and his staff are all quite friendly and even recognized me on my last trip! I appreciated that as I know that they must see thousands of people in their line of work. My mother was not happy about having to be weighed for the trip, but be prepared as this is part of the experience as they manage each flight by weight.

I found the cost to be quite reasonable and in line with the other flight companies around the island. I'm not much of a helicopter fan and so I found the small airplane option a bit more comfortable.

Each passenger is equipped with noise canceling headphones, through which your pilot will guide you through each site and the history of the island. For those new to Kauai, this is really nice and gives you a great overview of this magnificent place. The hanger is very easy to find, just past the main terminal at the Lihue airport. After your flight, be sure to take the drive further down the road, away from the main highway, to visit an old fishing pier and some lovely ocean scenery.

The first time that I took this flight, I was seated behind the pilot on the left side of the plane. NOT a good seat! They arrange passengers by weight, so please take into consideration that you might be the one positioned in the inner seat. Honestly, it is quite difficult to see much of anything from this seat and I found myself to be quite disappointed in the flight the first time that I went (hence the four star rating). Perhaps if they refunded part of the fee for the one who is instructed to sit in this "no view" seat, I might be more understanding. Thankfully, my second time around, I was placed in the seat on the view side.

You can actually get some great pics and video during this trip - and it's quite unique as you'll see some areas of the island not seen by most. Waterfalls, coastlines, mountains, towns, nature... you'll see it all.

If you're wanting a bird's-eye view of the island, this is a great and not-too-expensive way to do it! Just be ready if you get placed in the seat behind the pilot as views are limited.

I've taken a helicopter ride on Kauai before, and wasn't sure what to expect with a small airplane. I was surprised how smooth the ride was. The plane travels at a relatively slow speed and its easy to focus on the scenery and take pictures. The only downside, if there is one, is that a plane can't hover in front of waterfalls or cliffs like a helicopter. That said, the pilot will turn the plane around to ensure everyone gets good views of various scenes. He even made an extra loop above the ocean when he spotted a pod of whales.
Kauai is an absolutely gorgeous island and the combination of the ocean's waters, the NaPali cliffs, the beaches, and the inland canyons and waterfalls, make this trip quite memorable.

Review Title: breath taking tour of Kaua'i with propeller plane
Review Text: Generally enjoyed the propeller plane tour which takes you roughly clockwise over Kaua'i.  Felt comfortable the first 30 mins or so, then experienced a certain degree of dizziness and at times slight nausea likely caused by choppy gusts and possibly by the altitude (without the O2 compensation common in big jet liners).  Nice views of Po'ipu Beach, Waimea Canyon, and Hanalei Valley.  Saw Kilauea Lighthouse from the distance.  Unfortunately but not unusually, the visibility over the Na Pali Coast was cloudy, yet still breathtaking.  Mt. Wai'ale'ale was completely hidden in clouds, as it is said to be most of the time, but in turn the tour enabled many waterfall sightings.  In summary a fun way to see the island from above, but to the average person it is advisable to board the tour with an empty stomach and perhaps some prophylactic measures against motion sickness.  That said, the dizziness/nausea problem is probably not unique to AirVentures tours as I would anticipate a comparable level with the helicopter tours, and only 1 out of 6 passengers actually vomited.

We were each provided head phones so we could hear Harry's narrative tour of the island. I took lots of photos and they turned out great! Make sure you wear a dark color shirt if you're a shutter bug. It was more amazing than we ever dreamed, and we had been on a cruise around the island previously, and driven from one end of the island to the other several times. The air tour really put things in perspective, and it was neat to see things we would have never seen by car. We learned a great deal about the island from Harry, and even though we were pre-warned parts of the ride would be very bumpy (and they were) we would not hesitate to go again, or recommend this trip to anyone!

Review Text: When you are on a cruise with 4 days at 4 different Hawaiian Islands, you cannot do everything you would like. At Kauai, my wife and I decided that to get a sense of the Island, an airplane or helicopter ride would give you a good snapshot of the varied topography. We opted for the slower (and cheaper) one-hour airflight. We were not disappointed. We could both see well out of separate windows. We started off by following the south coast with its resorts and beaches and circled to see the famous Spouting Horn blowhole. Even though there was some cloud (to be expected in winter months) the Na Pali cliffs with inland waterfalls were awesome and the rain forest fascinating showing trees with different shades of green. We were also both able to be seated on the right side of the plane which is a must if you want to see anything. What I did notice is that the helicopters were MUCH lower than us and were able to go in and out of the canyons (Blue Hawaiian). Not sure it was worth $85/pp more, but something to consider.
The other 3 passengers on the plane were over an hour late arriving at the airport. It is not AirVentures fault, but it was very frustrating to lose that time. We were still able to do the full one-hour tour.
The sites are beautiful and Paul does a great job explaining what is below you. Airplane windows are great, but make sure to have a polarizing lens or you will have a lot of reflection.

On a side note: the Air and Ground tour actually charges you $4 MORE than if you do the two events seperate.

Review Title: The Best Part of Our Trip was the biplane ride on the last day! Awesome!
Review Text:
We had seen advertisements for air and helicopter tours. But never expected to see a biplane tour. We took both the standard plane tour, which was wonderful also. Then we spotted the biplane sign, I had to do it! We made an appointment and my brother-in-law Joe and I went for the ride with our pilot Nick DuBay. He was fabulous, also a flight instructor as I found out. It was like climbing into the Red Baran's plane to look for Snoopy!
We chose the duration and area we wanted to fly over. 45 minutes seemed enough, but I could have spent the whole afternoon wit Nick. We saw everything we saw from ground level, from an open cockpit, the pictures speak for themselves. Nick asked how daring we wanted to be, and we told him to 'go for it!'. We did several 'wing overs' pulling several 'G's' each time, we flew into the crater as far as Nick deemed to be safe. His flying skills kept any sign of air sickness out of the question. The price was right, it topped off two wonderful weeks in Kauai. If anyone misses the chance to fly in a biplane, they missed one thing that should be on anyone's 'Bucket List'. Great flying with you Nick! Mahalo! If anyone wants a more personal or in depth review, please feel free to contact me, Jack from Chicago, at chgoipa50@aol.com, happy to speak with you!

Review Title: I was the co-pilot on a plane over Kauai
Review Text:
I don't know how I got so lucky. I weighed the right amount. But I got to sit in the co-pilot seat. My friend asked the pilot to make sure I didn't try to fly. It looked like I could have if I had known how. Great views over the most beautiful island in the world. The views are just enough distant to provide good perspective. The view I treasured the most was just before we got to Waimea Canyon. We could see from the west into three waterfalls that fall 3,000 feet from Mt. Waialiali (sp?) the wettest place on earth. They seemed to spill from the clouds that shroud the top of the mountain. I had been on a helicopter tour of the island before but don't remember seeing that view.
The pilot, Harry, was wonderful, charming and informative and so helpful. The take off and landing were soft, not in the least scary or jarring. Unfortunately, one of the rear passengers got sick. It did not affect me, but the persons closer did not like that part of the trip. Very good experience for the money.

Review Text:
I've been wanting to go on a helicopter tour my whole life and found a 2-for-1 coupon in my hotel's pamphlet for Air Ventures. I booked a Sunday morning tour for two and asked what kind of helicopter we'd be flying. "It's actually an airplane, an AirVan," said the friendly voice.

I considered canceling - doesn't everyone see Hawaii from a helicopter? Isn't that the "it" thing to do?

We kept our time slot and showed up early. There were seven of us scheduled to fly together, everyone amiable and sharing their travel stories. The flight lasted almost an hour - and we saw EVERYTHING. Also, when I asked the pilot to show us something specifically, he nodded and made sure to include it along our route, even doubling back a few miles to point out the open-air cave along the Na Pali Coast.

When we returned, we spoke to a man from our hotel who paid twice as much to go on a helicopter ride for half the time and saw a third of what we saw (and if I haven't mentioned it, we saw the entire island). His wife was none too pleased at being left behind, and he said the helicopter ride was incredibly bumpy - hard to photograph. My photographs came out spectacular.

I got an incredibly great price on this, and I think Air Ventures would lose money if everyone found the coupon I did. But if you're on a budget and enjoy star treatment, do your research ahead of time and expect to be rewarded.

Review Title: Misleading waste of time and money. Will be contacting priceline

One of the girls on the right side was kind enough to snap a few pictures for me and also thought it was foolish how they arranged us. Oh there is Julia Roberts house and there is Pierce Brosnan's place. (The tot does not know who they are.) I will never know with my view of the ocean, wing, and white bar holding the wing on. This was absolute crap. Do yourself a favor and wait until you are here and book a helicopter tour. I have been sick at my stomach all day from this tiny plane and also just feel very ripped off. I cannot believe the pilot gave a tot a cherry seat and stuck me where he did either. A short girl getting to spread out in front. I had a 20 dollar tip ready but I left tipping nothing. I guess I will go blow 15 on a beer at the St. Regis where I am staying. Did not like the reference that it was foolish to spend 15 on a beer. What was foolish was this plane ride. I think I should get refunded as I have booked a copter tour tomorrow and have to drive all the way back to that side of the island to get a decent tour. Review Text:
My wife and I took a 50 minute air tour with AirVentures and were flown around the island by Captain Harry in one of their two Gippsland GA-8 AirVan single engine fixed wing aircraft. The plane holds about 8 people and has high wings (over the plane) and large slightly curved windows which allow for good viewing. Do wear dark clothing without patterns to reduce glare off the windows when taking photos. I got to sit in the co-pilot's seat which was an added treat.

Captain Harry provided a good running commentary on the surroundings. We flew southwest from Lihue just north of the southern coast, over the Waimea Canyon area, and then up the Na Pali coast. On the north side we flew around the Hanalei Bay area and then cut across the island back towards Lihue. We saw a gorgeous ground rainbow as we were coming in for a landing.

If you are prone to air sickness, it is highly recommended that you take some medication prior to boarding the plane. My wife struggled with air sickness during the flight. Also, if you are looking for up close views of the waterfalls on the island, the helicopter tours are probably the way to go. We saw several helicopters that were providing their occupants with very close views of waterfalls while we were several thousand feet above them.

All in all, this was an excellent trip and good value. AirVentures provides a good overview of the island and allows you to locate areas that you might want to see from ground level. Do try to schedule this trip early on in your visit.

Each corner we turned brought another wonderful vista into view, with gorgeous blue and white coves and magnificent waterfalls everywhere we looked. I would recommend anyone take this once in a lifetime flight who wants to see a part of this amazing world God has created in the only way possible to really enjoy the full extent of its beauty.

Review Title: Kauai takes the Hawai'i experience up a level or two, AirVentures lets you experience Kauai in a way that a car can't!
Review Text:
My wife and I have wanted to visit Hawai'i for a long time, but weren't able to until recently, when I started working in Honolulu. Everyone I work with heaps accolades and superlatives on just about everything - rightfully so! After a few weeks of living in Waikiki, we finally got a chance to see another island, and came to Kauai - the Garden Island. What does one do to describe Kauai when you've tried to use every maximum superlative you can muster to describe O'ahu and then come to Kauai - and find it to be everything you've found over there - and so much more!!!? It's quieter, more beautiful, not crowded, and has attractions that do not exist on O'ahu. The majesty of Waimea Canyon does bring to mind, immediately, the sweeping vistas of Arizona's Grand Canyon, but with different colors. When finished with the Grand Canyon, though, you just can't drive a little further up the road and see something like the fantastic view of the Napali Coast that lies a few minutes north of the Wiamea Canyon.
Then there are the number of small towns dotting Kauai's coastline, each with it's own suite of local shops, places to eat - and beaches!
It's all almost overwhelming!
Then you meet the people at AirVentures and take an aerial tour of the island, and see all those places you've driven to, and some that you wished you could have - and you see everything from the perspective you can only get from the air! The Napali coast, the plantations living and abandoned, the houses of those we've seen on the screen, the impossible greenery that's everywhere, the sereneness permeates you! Review Title: Absolutely the Best Way to Experience Kaui
Review Text:
Just got back from a cruise in Hawaii. The highlight of our trip was the "Big Kahuna" sightseeing flight around Kaui with Air Ventures Hawaii. We were picked up near our cruise ship port in Nawiliwili, Kaui and shuttled to nearby Lihue Airport for our flight. From the start, you could see that this is a top-notch operation. My daughter and I checked in with the staff and the pilot, Harry, quickly introduced himself to us and the two other gentlemen going on the flight.
We had contemplated going on one of the many helicopter tours availailable in Kaui, but instead decided to go on one of Air Ventures airplanes. They are very comfortable GA- 8 high wing airplanes with excellent visibility. They are quieter than helicopters, can fly very slowly so you don't miss anything (our whole flight was done at 90 -110 knots and we varied our touring altitude from 500 ft to 4000 ft) , and everyone on board gets a window seat. Most importantly, the aircraft are much more economical to operate, which makes the fares much lower than with a helicopter trip.
Harry did a great job of narrating the flight via headphones. We flew clockwise around the coastline, flew directly over our docked cruise ship, then descended into Waimea Canyon for great pictures. We then ascended over the top of the canyon and down along the Na'pali Coast for unbelievable views. Finally, we came around the other side of Kaui and into the Hanelei Valley. The trip took about 70 minutes and we got the most comprehensive tour of Kaui one can possibly imagine. Back on the ground, they were nice enough to give us a ride to the rental car facility.Finished the day off with a high speed catamaran ride back to the Na'pali Coast with their Air and Sea Combo. An excellent end to an excellent day.

Review Text:
On our recent trip to Kauai I really wanted to take an aerial tour of the island, but was discouraged by the helicopter companies policy of gouging big people for a ride. I'm 6'6" and just shy of 300 lbs, and the helicopter operators charge you for an extra seat.
I discovered AirVentures online, and for just a little over a hundred dollars had a GREAT air tour.
The staff was super friendly....very Aloha!! I got the seat in back right by the door, with no seat in front of it, and was able to stretch my legs fully out on the ride, and was able to easily see out of both sides of the plane. Our pilot was really cool, and talked with us a lot during the trip.
The ride itself was awesome!! The headphones made the noise minimal, and communications were easy. The takeoff was smooth as can be, and the flight very comfortable. There were a few bumpy parts here and there, but really nothing major. We saw all of the sights from Poipu, up Waimea Canyon, all along Napali, the North Shore beaches, Hanalei Valley, and inland to Waileilei, then over the East Shore before landing back in Lihue.
While we didn't dive into the canyons like the helicopters do (although watching the helicopters below us, I thought they got a bit too close for comfort) we flew low enough to see everything in great detail. And there was no "wasted" time flying over the water as somebody had previously posted.
AirVentures Kauai is an excellent value....if you dont want to pay the exorbinant charges the helicopter companies charge, book this flight....you WILL NOT be disappointed!!
One last thing, if it is the only splurge you take on your trip....do not miss flying over Kauai. It is honestly the most beautiful sight I have ever seen.

Review Title: One of the must-dos, totally worth the money
Review Text:
I was originally planning for a boat tour to the Na Pali coast and only changed my mind in the last minute. Na Pali is one of the most beautiful areas of Kauai, and it's inaccessible by car, so you'll really have to plan to sail, fly or walk the 11-mi trail to see the coast line. I was so lucky to be able to get a seat on the busy Christmas eve. It was a beautiful day, and the ride was just so perfect. The staff at Air Ventures were extremely friendly, and I was very impressed that Captain Harry took everyone like a family tour, as opposed to a paid guided tour. He explained every place we flew by, detoured to the water and pointed out whales--I never knew it's so amazing to see the whales from the air. You can actually see them under the water, and we were even luckier to see a whale doing a flip, making a huge splash of water. Then we flew down the famous Kalalau Valley, spent 15-20min in the Na Pali coast area, and then continued to Hanalei valley, and before we returned to the airport, Captain Harry flow around the beautiful Wailua falls so everyone got a close-up views of the falls (much larger than what you'd see from the road).

I've taken flightseeings in Alaska and Hawaii, and my personal experience is when the weather is good, it's absolutely worth every penny--even if you found the price may be enough for you to fly a round trip across the continental US :) But I'd always give it a second thought if the weather isn't good. And finally, Air Ventures operates an air van (or more), which flights higher than helicopters, so you won't get a chance to fly by the water falls, but you don't really miss anything, and considering that the price is probably 50% lower, it's an unbeatable deal. BTW, everyone has a window seat on the air van, and Air Ventures keep their windows spotless; while on a 6-passenger helicopter, only 3 people get window seats.

If the trip was over it would be a great trip, but we then flew on over the dense jungle and the north and the mountainous volcano region. This is the wettest area on earth, but was dry in our biplane. The down the east coast back to the airport. The pilot then took our photographs in and next to the plane. I don't recall the particulars about the plane and helicopter rides, but I think we will always remember the biplane trip of Kauai. I would certainly recommend the biplane trip of Kauai if it was the only thing you did while there. When I think of Kauai, I think of the jungle chickens and the biplane ride.

Review Title: Great value and an amazing way to see Kauai
Review Text:
Originally, my family and I were going to go on a helicopter tour. We decided to go with Air Ventures for a couple of reasons: 1. It was a lot less expensive and 2. The way the plane is configured, everyone has a great window seat. Review Title: Best Way to View the Entire Island
Review Text:
We did this on our third day and really were glad that we did. We did the 1-hour tour and got the free DVD for booking online. (By the way, the DVD is worth it if you book online and get it for free, but not for the $20 or whatever you had to pay for it, it's only like 20 min. long and doesn't have that great of quality, but was a nice gift for us since it was free!) This was something my husband was adamant about doing and since I get really motion sick, I wasn't originally too keen on it. In fact, he originally started wanting to do a doors-off helicopter ride and I was excited to find Air Ventures had such great reviews so that I could suggest this as an alternative to the helicopter, which went over well and I think he's very happy that we did it this way.

You really get to see the entire island from above and get some of the history from your guide. Our guide/pilot wasn't as talkative as we would have liked, but really no one on the plane was asking questions or talking to him either, so I think it's understandable that it turned out that way. And most of the sights speak for themselves. You get to see the coffee fields, all of the fabulous/famous beaches of the island, waterfalls, Waimea Canyon, where Jurassic Park/Raiders of the Lost Ark was filmed, etc etc etc --- it is really all encompassing and I would recommend it.

The people that run it and were the pilots were SUPER nice as well, which really makes for an awesome trip, especially because I was a little nervous about flying in such a small plane.

As for the motion sickness, I did ok for a half hour and then was feeling really ill for the second half, but I never actually got sick and imagine it's MUCH better than a helicopter ride would have been. And they were very sweet about it as well, offering watering and where I could sit to cool off, so that was much appreciated.

I think this is a must do for those on Kauai, it's so cool to see all of the places from above and then spend the rest of the week exploring from the ground or water, very cool!

Review Text:

Wir haben den großen Rundflug über die gesamte Insel gemacht. Der Pilot war sehr nett und konnte viel über die Insel erzählen. In der Maschine haben 7 Personen (inkl Pilot) Platz und man hat von überall einen herrlichen Ausblick.

Aus diesem Grund würde ich beim nächsten Mal einen Helikopter ausprobieren. Diese Entscheidung, muss aber jeder nach seinen individuellen Einschätzungen vornehmen.

Review Title: A must for those serious about touring Kauai
Review Text:
Many thanks to an excellent flight crew for making this an unforgettable experience. Our skilled pilot ( Harry ), was also great at describing all the sites and their historical background. Michelle, was professional and friendly, taking care of all the preliminary tasks to prepare for the flight.
This flight was very special to me as I am a commercial pilot/aircraft owner/ aerial photographer. I would like to point out some of the advantages of this fixed wing aircraft over helicopters. Most significant is the lower cost to operate the aircraft, sipping only 13 gallons of fuel per hour. Maintenance costs are much lower than helicopters. These reduced costs result in a lower cost to the passengers. That’s not all, this GA-8 Airvan delivers a silky smooth ride with little vibration, as opposed to constant vibration in helicopters, very important for sharp photographs. Every passenger gets a clean bubble window to view through, and these are always kept clean.
This type of aerial tour is the only way to view many of the sites around the island, as many are inaccessible by car, trail, or even boat.
This aerial tour was a highlight of my stay in Kauai.

But, after all the driving and hiking we only had a few hours to spare on the island. What would be the best way to use those last few hours? Kauai Air Ventures tour. The best. We saw the Na Pali Coast (a place only accessible by boat or airplane), DOZENS of waterfalls, the famous rock arch on the beach, and we flew in and out of canyons and as close to the mountains as possible. Basically the tour flew us around the whole island. PLUS, the cost is almost half of what the helicopter tours charge. We felt very safe. And our pilot, who was very knowledgeable, was able to answer nearly all of our questions. He even pinpointed the exact locations of where movies such as 6 Days/7 Nights and Jurassic Park III were filmed! All in all, we felt our money was well spent! We would definitely do the tour again if we had the time.

Review Title: The Best Sightseeing Activity on Kauai !!
Review Text:
If you want to see Kauai from the air... the Air Ventures hour tour is the way to do it. This is way better than a helicopter tour (which we have done)... quieter, more comfortable, you see way more and you get the opportunity to take great pictures. This was our favorite activity in 2 weeks of sightseeing on Maui and Kauai.

Our pilot, Joel, was wonderful. They have headphones and mikes so the pilot can point out the various sites, as well as allowing you to ask questions and share things you see. Our trip started at the Lihue airport. Our take off was quick and you felt like you were floating when airborne. The plane is made in Australia and can hold up to 6 people and the pilot. There is lots of space in the plane, the seats are comfy even for big people and we didn't feel cramped at all. There were only 4 of us and the pilot when we took our trip. Everyone gets a large window to look out of and it's easy to look out both sides of the plane. The plane flys slowly at altitutes of 500-3000 ft above the island depending on where you are.

Our tour took us over the Nawiliwili harbor, down along the coast to Poipu, on to Waimea with views over Port Allen and Barking Sands Beach. We then went over the Waimea canyon and saw many waterfalls and the awesome views of the canyon itself. We then continued on to the Na Pali Coast...Incredible from the air!! As we rounded the point to Ke'e Beach (also known as Bali Hai Beach), it was fun to see the wonderful beaches we had visited earlier in the week. We continued on past Kileauea Lighthouse and down the beach studded coast. Just prior to landing, we flew over the Wailua River and saw Wailua Falls from the air (an awesome waterfall which I included in my pictures).

Too soon we were landing and saying Thank You for a wonderful trip. We took over 300 pictures during our flight and we said to each other as we got out "You wouldn't have to twist my arm to get me to do it again!"

This is an A+++ tour, great people, great plane, great scenery. What more can I say.... Just do it !!

Review Text: Yesterday my wife, a friend, and I went on a flight over Kauai riding in a fixed wing aircraft flown by an experienced pilot from Air Ventures.  We debated flying in a helicopter instead of the fixed wing aircraft, because a helicopter can hover over a scenic location, but opted for the lower cost aircraft.  We had heard that the Air Van aircraft, which seats 7 passengers and flies at about 115 - 120 mph offers plenty of time to take pictures of waterfalls and other scenic spots.  Each passenger is seated next to an optically clear plastic window and is provided an opportunity to photograph locations of interest.  I was using my new digital SLR and got some great photos.  The flight takes an hour and the plane travels (at least our flight did) in a clockwise direction around the island, primarily along the coast line and over the Waimea Canyon (the Grand Canyon of the Pacific), traveling over the Hanalei Valley when returning to Lihue.  My wife and I had toured much of the island by vehicle on a trip to Kauai with two other friends just last January, but seeing the canyon and some of the waterfalls that we had seen from the road-side access was not nearly as exciting as the view from the aircraft.  We particularly enjoyed flying over the Napali coast (western shoreline) and seeing all of the waterfalls.  Our flight was on a relatively clear day after several days of intermittent heavy rainfall, so the waterfalls were spectacular and abundant.  The pilot was very good about pointing out the sites and telling us historical anecdotes about various scenic locations.  The noise-canceling headphones and microphones provided each passenger enabled us to hear him clearly and ask questions.  He was an excellent pilot, considerate about minimizing turbulence by flying above it or moving away from the cliffs, and very knowledgeable about Kauai.  In short, I would strongly recommend taking the Air Ventures aircraft flight as providing one of the best ways to see all of the major sites of interest on the entire island.  We all enjoyed the flight and felt it provided more than any other recreational experience during this vacation.

Review Title: An Aerial View of Kauai, Hiwaii
Review Text: On September 24, 2008, our party of six boarded an Air Ventures Hawaii Airvan fixed-wing aircraft for a one-hour tour of the island of Kauai.  The flight provided us with some of the most dramatic scenery one can imagine!  Taking off from the Lihue Airport on the southeastern shore of the island, our pilot flew to the south shore, taking in the small towns along the rugged coast line.  The pilot provided plenty of narration without being overly talkative.  The noise reduction headsets had individual microphones, so each of us could ask questions or comment on the scenery below.  Turning to the west, our flight took us over the Waimea Canyon area known as the "Grand Canyon of Hawaii."  It lived up to its name, as the rugged mountains plunged into vast canyons, lined with waterfalls and variegated formations of lava, weathered by several million years of rain and wind.  The northwest shore provided stunning views of the NaPali Coast.  These 4,000 foot mountains look like ribbons of green as they drop directly to the sea.  This was the most spectacular sight of the flight!  We continued up the valleys around Princeville, ending up near Mount Waialeale, the wettest spot on earth with 450 inches of annual rainfall.  The flight was smooth, with only minor bounces from the mountain wind currents.  Visibility from the large windows was excellent, and all six of us were able to capture some outstanding photos.  The flight was slow enough to have a great view of the island, yet fast enough to get us completely around the island in exactly one hour.  We would recommend this flight as an excellent way to see the beautiful garden island of Kauai.

Review Title: A true highlight of our trip!
Review Text:
I wanted to take an air tour of Kauai but wasn't sure if I wanted a helicopter or airplane. Being a bit of a history buff, when the google search brought up "Tropical Biplanes", I knew this was what I was looking for!

It starts with you boarding a cherry red, double cockpit biplane. My wife and I sat in the front cockpit, the pilot in the back cockpit. We were supplied with cloth helmets, goggles, and radio set (reminding me of the old Battle of Midway movie). These were needed as the cockpit was open air (you do have a windscreen to protect you)!

The flight was awesome! Being an open cockpit, you had an almost unobstructed view in every direction. I loved sticking my head over the side and looking straight down at the ocean. One disadvantage of the plane versus a helicopter, was that we were not able to get close to many of the falls or anything.

Our pilot was great. He was very professional and friendly. He provided us plenty of information about the sites without being overbearing or cheesy. When he found out what beach we were married on, he banked the plane so we could get some great pictures from the air!

If you are looking for a flight a bit more adventurous than the usual airplane/helicopter tour (and want to feel the wind in your face!), I would highly recommend Tropical Biplanes.

Review Title: See Kauai from the air with Air Ventures
Review Text:
Flying with Air Ventures is not just a cheaper alternative to taking the more expensive helicopter tours!

You get a full hour tour with a great guide and pilot (Joel) to tour all of the major sights of the island and see things you cannot see from the ground.

The plane is specially designed for low speed flying and much quieter than the helicopters. You get a headset and microphone to enable two way communication with the pilot.

You will see the harbor, the entire western coast (NaPali), Kalalau Valley, Hanalei Bay, Princeville, numerous waterfalls, the Powerline Trail, Mt. Waialeale, coffee plantations, Wailua Falls, and many other sights.

This was our fourth trip to Kauai but our first time to see the island from the air and it is well worth the money spent. Don't book with any other airplane or helicopter tour. Then report your experiences back to this website!
